## Chapter 25: The Golden Ball

### Notes

#### Chapter Summary

The group attends a party thrown by the White Lotus, where feelings are simmering below the surface, emotions are at an all-time high, and shocking secrets are revealed.

#### Chapter Notes

TW: Blood, knives, gunshots, threats.

This is one of my favorite chapters of the entire fic! I absolutely love a party scene, especially in a murder mystery! I had so much fun writing this one (and describing everyone's outfits), and I really hope you all enjoy it! Happy reading:)

### Text

Katara stared at her reflection in Zuko’s mirror. She looked...strange.

It wasn’t that she didn’t love the gown she was wearing. On the contrary, she absolutely adored it. It was simple but stunning, made of a silky fabric that seemed to flow down her body like a river, and that slowly faded from nearly white at the top to nearly black at the bottom, with every shade of blue in between. It was easily one of the fanciest things she had ever put on.

It had also belonged to her mother. That was the strange part.

She was soon pulled out of her mirror trance by loud knocks on the door. “What?” she called. “I’m almost ready!” She leaned down and tightened the straps on her silver flats, just to be sure.

Sokka poked his head in. He, too, had dressed for the occasion. Katara was pretty sure that the tie he was wearing over his pale blue shirt was the only tie he owned. Still, he looked nice in it. The tie was the same purple-blue color that their father loved. Katara was sure that it was intentional.

“You look good.”

“So do you,” replied Sokka. Then he grinned, wiggling his eyebrows. “I bet *Yue* will think so, too.”

It was as though a rain cloud floated into the room and came to a stop right above Katara’s head at the simple mention of Yue’s name. She cared about her friend, and would never abandon her, but she wished *so much* that things could be different. She’d only wished harder for one thing in her entire life. “I don’t want to talk about that.”

Sokka blinked. “Really? I was sure you two had something going on.”

Katara laughed bitterly. “Yeah, that was a stupid idea.”

“Oh.” Sokka’s voice was so soft that it cracked, making it sound strange, but Katara appreciated the gesture as he placed his hand on her shoulder. “Well, she’s missing out.”

Katara smiled. As she turned towards her brother, her dangling silver earrings glittered in the mirror. “Thanks, Sokka.”

Zuko sighed, checking his watch, as he stood outside his sister’s room. It wasn’t abnormal for Azula to be insanely perfectionistic about her appearance, but that didn’t make it any less infuriating. “Azula, just put on that little red dress I know you packed! We don’t have all day for this!”

“Not in a million years!” called Azula. “That dress is *tiny* and *impractical* and I can’t do *anything* in it! I know there’s something else!”

“Well, find your *something* *else* quickly! The White Lotus party starts in half an hour, and they won’t let us in if we’re too late!”

The door flew open, and Azula stepped into the light. “I found it.”

Zuko couldn’t not stare. Azula looked so incredibly *different* that he almost couldn’t process it. He had grown up seeing his sister at parties, in long dresses and high heels, with her hair in its usual tight topknot, and layers upon layers of makeup applied by assistants hired by their father.

The Azula standing before him had her hair in some sort of coiled-half-ponytail, and a large portion of it was hanging down around her face. She wore slim black pants, and a red silk shirt with a black sash that wrapped around her body, framing her waist perfectly. On her feet was a pair of black leather boots. She had put on makeup, but a thousand times less than Zuko was used to.

Azula smirked. “Do you like it? I had nothing remotely practical in my suitcase, so Mai lent this to me a while ago. It’s a little long, since she’s significantly taller than I am, but I think it suits me quite nicely, don’t you?”

“Father would kill you if he saw you in that,” was all Zuko could think to say.

Azula scanned him up and down. His uncle had made him wear a suit, and he kept untucking things because it felt uncomfortable. “He would kill *you* if he saw you like *that* .”

Zuko shrugged. “He would probably kill me anyway.”

Azula laughed. Of course *she* would enjoy dark humor.

She turned and studied her reflection in the window. Zuko couldn’t help but think that, under the lights, in this outfit, she looked more like *herself* than he’d seen in a pretty long time.

“Well, Father isn’t here right now, is he?”

Sokka and Katara came out of the other room. The minute Katara saw Azula, she grinned and clapped her hands excitedly. “You look fantastic!”

Azula smiled back, a genuine one. “So do you. You look like...some sort of ethereal aquatic being.”

Katara looked slightly confused, but thanked her anyway.

“What are you doing here?” Azula asked Suki when they arrived at the party, as the rest of the group ran off to join the quick dancers spinning around the room. “How did you manage to get invited to a *White Lotus* event?”

Suki smiled, but her smile was weak. Azula could tell that she was still upset over the events of Lake Laogai (and who could blame her?) With her deep green tuxedo, perfect makeup, and sophisticated bob, she looked as put-together as ever, but Azula could see the fragility underneath her façade. She’d seen the same fragility under a façade in the mirror for years. It was only now that it was starting to fade. “Apparently the White Lotus heard about me helping you investigate the Dai Li, and they invited me as a sort of reward.” She didn’t seem too thrilled.

Azula grabbed two small glasses of champagne from a passing waiter and handed one to Suki. “And are you happy about this?”

Suki shrugged. “I don’t know. I mean, I guess I’ve already betrayed the Dai Li. Why not go all the way?”

“Do you still want their approval?”

Suki shook her head. “Not after everything they did. But...they’re the closest thing I have to a family. If I betray them, what’s left?”

Azula shrugged, sitting down next to her. “I can’t tell you what the perfect solution is for you. But in my experience, even if you think you only have one family, there’s usually at least one person out there who will accept the real you, not a façade or an ideal. And if you’re lucky enough, they’ll give you a chance.” Her eyes wandered over to Zuko, who was chatting with Aang on the other side of the room. “Those people can be family, friends, or…” she turned to look directly at Suki, “something else. But if you want to find those people, you need to first accept that you *want* to. If you spend your whole life trying to fit into a box you don’t want to fit into, you’ll never find those people you’re looking for. So, you need to let them know that you’re looking.”

Suki took a sip of champagne, staring at the ceiling. The fast music that the band had been playing when they entered was slowly morphing into a slow waltz. Azula could hear a string orchestra playing, and the dancers were slowing down, the crowd on the dance floor becoming sparser.

“I never knew you gave such good advice,” said Suki after a moment.

Azula laughed. “I don’t,” she admitted. “That was only from personal experience.” She glanced over to where Zuko was standing. “But if you tell anyone I said that, you’ll have to face me in battle, and trust me when I say that I will show no mercy.”

“Well, I definitely don’t want to do that,” said Suki. “You should go,” she added, pointing to Katara, who was beckoning to her across the room. “I’ll think about what you said. But Azula?”

“Yes?”

“Maybe you should take your own advice.” Suki’s eyes wandered over to Zuko, then to Ty Lee, who was coming down the stairs. “On more than one account.”

Azula tried to hide the blush that appeared on her face as she waved to Suki and crossed the room to where Katara was standing. “Are we plotting something now? I’m all ears.”

Katara laughed, though Azula noted that she was making an active effort not to look at Yue, who was standing on the other side of the room. “Actually, we *are* plotting something.” She gestured over to Zuko, who was standing by a pillar and trying to look brooding (at least, that’s what it seemed like he was doing), and Sokka, who was showing Aang something that involved a lot of shrimp. “I think those two could use a little dance lesson, don’t you?”

Azula smirked. This had the potential to be *very* entertaining. “You know what, I really think they could.”

The string orchestra was reaching its climax as Azula made her way over to Zuko and held out her hand. “Zuko, I seem to recall that you had a taste for dancing as a child.”

Zuko’s face turned red, but he took her hand anyway. “You’re remembering wrong.”

“Don’t be embarrassed about it,” said Azula. “Father made us learn so that we could impress at parties. You were quite good at it, as I recall.” She caught Katara’s eye from across the ballroom, as Katara pulled her own brother out onto the dance floor. Azula smirked as they began to spin towards each other.

“Doesn’t really fit with the detective image, though,” replied Zuko, spinning Azula around. He spun her so fast that Azula nearly tripped, but she held her own. Dancing had never come naturally to her like it had for Zuko, but she’d become good at hiding that fact, using simpler steps when no one was watching.

“You never know,” replied Azula, spinning Zuko around to where Katara and Sokka were dancing, then letting go of Zuko’s hand and turning so that he and Sokka were facing each other. Her own hand reached out and found Katara’s, and the two of them began spinning away. “Perhaps you’ll need to solve a murder at a masquerade ball someday.”

Giggling, the two girls came to a stop over by Suki. Azula was about to suggest that the three of them go find some food when she spotted Ty Lee walking towards her. Remembering the incident in the park the previous day, she looked away from her, her face reddening against her will as she stared at the floor.

“Azula?”

Against her better judgement, Azula glanced up. She shouldn’t have. Ty Lee looked absolutely breathtaking. Her braid had been coiled into a bun at the base of her neck, and her dress was pale pink, all soft waves and cascading tulle. She looked like a fairy. There was even a small pink flower in her hair.

“Can we talk?”

Against her better judgement (again), Azula nodded, and let Ty Lee lead her out onto the dance floor as the strings faded away to a soft rhapsody, with only the mournful notes of a violin and the plucking of a lute. Ty Lee placed her hands around Azula’s waist, and they began to sway.

“So,” said Sokka, his voice cracking, as he attempted to find his footing and not step on Zuko’s feet for a third time. He had always been a horrible dancer, “we’re...uh, dancing, huh?” He could feel nervous adrenaline coursing through his body. “How did that happen?” he finished awkwardly.

Zuko seemed just as mortified as he was. His face was flushed, and he couldn’t even look Sokka in the eye. “Yeah, I...guess that’s pretty weird.”

“We can stop if you want!” Sokka cried quickly. “I...don’t want to make this too awkward, or...aah!”

Sokka had tripped over Zuko’s shoe and was about to fall flat on his face when arms wrapped around his waist, spinning him around. Zuko was holding onto him, keeping him from falling. Their faces were suddenly only inches apart.

So much for not making it awkward.

Laughing nervously, Sokka slowly got to his feet. They stood still in the middle of the dance floor for what felt like hours, not knowing what to say. “Uh...thanks,” he managed after a while. “I’m a pretty terrible dancer. You...probably noticed that.” He forced a laugh, but it just sounded like he was choking.

Zuko didn’t laugh. He stared intensely at his hands for a second before extending one to Sokka. “I can teach you how to dance.” There was silence, and Zuko’s face turned bright red. “I mean, if you want me to!”

Sokka smirked. Seeing that Zuko was also a little uncomfortable made this slightly more bearable. “I didn’t know you could dance.”

Zuko rubbed his hand through his hair. “Yeah, my father made me learn. Here.” He thrust his hand out again, and hesitantly, Sokka took it, ignoring the heat in his face. This felt so *weird* .

“Okay,” said Zuko, grabbing Sokka’s other hand and putting it on his shoulder. His hand wrapped around Sokka’s waist, almost like it had when Sokka had tripped. Sokka was suddenly very aware of the music, the violin and lute playing in unison. “All you have to do is just follow my lead. We move in threes.” He stepped backwards, then sideways, then forwards, and somehow, Sokka found himself following along to the beat of the music. It almost felt like they were floating. If you ignored the fact that Sokka was literally shaking, that is.

“You just do the three steps over and over again.” Zuko offered Sokka a genuine smile, and despite his nerves, Sokka smiled back. “That’s all there is to it.”

After Azula disappeared into the crowd with Ty Lee, Katara found herself near Suki. She sat down next to the other girl, who was staring off into nothingness, deep in thought. “You okay?”

Suki glanced up, seeming to just notice Katara for the first time. “I...am, I guess. I’m just *really* worried about Mai.”

Katara sighed, wrapping her arms around her friend. It was sad how easy it was to forget what had happened to Mai. With all the violence that kept chasing them, it all felt like one big blur sometimes. Katara hated herself for it. “We’ll get her back. I promise.”

“I hope so,” Suki sighed. “It’s just...I keep wishing she were here.”

“She would hate this.”

Suki nodded, laughing. “She really would.”

Katara caught a glimpse of the look in Suki’s eyes. It was an expression she recognized from her own face, and she knew how much it hurt. “Do you think...is it worth asking yourself *why* you miss her so much?”

Suki sighed, slumping against a pillar. “It’s funny. I always thought I hated her, but I never really knew her at all. And now that I *do* know her, I really like her. She understands me in a way that not a lot of people do.”

“You enjoy her company.”  
Suki toyed with her necklace. “I...I think it’s more than that. I don’t know,” she groaned. “I...I’ve been connected to the Dai Li for so long. I don’t really know what to do about stuff like this.”

“I can’t tell you what you’re feeling,” Katara admitted. “But I can promise you this; if you really want to get Mai back, you will. Because you’re *you* , and you’re strong, and you’re brave, and you kick serious ass, and you never give up.”

Suki smiled, even though she still seemed lost in thought. “Thanks, Katara. I’ll think on that.”

“Katara?”

Katara recognized the voice, and pointedly looked away. Sensing the tension, Suki gave Katara a wave and walked off to another corner of the room, leaving them alone.

“Katara, please. I just want to talk to you.”

Katara continued looking away.

“You *promised* me that you would be my friend. Don’t break your promise. At least look me in the eye and tell me the truth if you don’t want to be friends anymore.”

Katara sighed, rising and looking Yue right in the eye. There was a part of her brain that registered how gorgeous Yue looked: she was wearing a dress of pale blue, white, and silver with long sleeves and a high neckline that looked as though it was made of snow and ice. She ignored that part of her brain. “Fine. You want to talk to me? Let’s dance.”

Still angry, she thrust out her hand and pulled Yue onto the dance floor. Despite her anger, Katara could feel them slide into synchronization almost seamlessly, without even trying. It was as though they were gliding over an ice rink, but they were incapable of falling.

“What did you want to talk about?”

Yue sighed. Even under the lights of the dance floor, she could see the tears in Yue’s eyes. “I...I wanted to apologize for the other day. You were right. I shouldn’t have asked you to be a secret. It wasn’t fair of me, and...I’m sorry.” Even with the violin and the lute playing in the background, Katara could still hear the weight in Yue’s voice. “I hope you’re still okay with being my friend. You're amazing, and...I just don’t want to lose you.”

Katara squeezed Yue’s hand. “You could never lose me. I just...I wish we had the chance to be more. I don’t like seeing you so unhappy.”

Another tear fell from Yue’s eyes. “I do too, Katara. I really do.”

Katara could give Yue a lecture about agency in her own life, but this wasn’t the time. She just held her hand while they danced, as best as she could. It wasn’t perfect, and it wasn’t what they wanted, but it was something.

Or so she thought. Out of the crowd, Hahn suddenly appeared between them, draping his arm around Yue’s shoulders, and shoving Katara away. Surprised, Katara was unable to keep her balance, and fell against the wall, groaning as her head slammed into the wood.

“Come on, babe,” she heard Hahn mutter to Yue. “We have better things to do.”

Yue cast one glance back at Katara before they disappeared into the crowd. Her eyes were full of wist and longing, and it was all Katara could do not to run after her.

In the end, they’d only danced for half a song.

“You’re a good dancer,” was all Azula could think to say. There were so many things she wanted to say. *I’m sorry I left you alone. I never wanted to. I care about you more than anything. But trust* *me, it’s for your own good. You’re falling for a monster. I’m protecting you because I can’t stand* *to see you hurt.*

But she didn’t say any of that. She just kept swaying, letting Ty Lee steer her through the crowd.

“I’m not that good,” replied Ty Lee. “You just have to feel the music.” Two spots of pink appeared on her face. “Listen, Azula, about the other day...if I was pressuring you into something you didn’t want, I just…”

“Stop.” Azula couldn’t stop herself from speaking. Seeing Ty Lee look so guilty was too hard. What was she *becoming* ? Had she lost *all* control?

Perhaps she had. But if she had, why did it feel so *good* ?

“You never pressured me. You never did *anything* wrong. This…” she sighed. She hated being wrong. “This was my fault.”

“Right,” said Ty Lee. For the first time ever, Azula caught an undertone of bitter sarcasm in her voice. “It’s not you, it’s me, right? That’s what you mean?”

“Exactly!” replied Azula, but her relief quickly faded when she saw Ty Lee’s face fall. “No, not like that! Look…” Azula took a deep breath. “You’re amazing, and believe me, I don’t say that every day. But I don’t think I should do what I think it is that you want right now.” She sighed. “I’m sorry I let it go this far. I understand if you don’t want to talk to me anymore.”

To her surprise, Ty Lee pulled her into a hug, as they continued spinning. “Azula, don’t be silly. I’m happy to be your friend. I never needed more. Nothing is going to change that.”

*Happy to be your friend* . *I never needed more.* Did that mean that she’d never felt the same things Azula did, or at least *thought* she did? Had Azula misinterpreted the whole thing?

Probably. After all, Azula knew what kind of person she was. It had been a rather unattainable dream to begin with.

But, somehow, she *did* have Ty Lee as a friend. And she wasn’t going to be silly enough to misinterpret her signals or let her go again. She was special.

Instinctively, Azula squeezed Ty Lee’s hand, and they kept on dancing to the rhapsody.

Katara barely noticed when the rhapsody everyone had been dancing to came to an end. She was on the stairs, sitting and staring into space like Suki had been doing earlier. Except, unlike Suki, she wasn’t confused. She was pretty sure this was more like heartbreak.

It broke her heart that she felt so much love for someone she couldn’t give it to, and it broke her heart to see the person she loved so much suffering, and be unable to help her.

It broke her heart to feel so goddamn *broken* .

She hadn’t even realized she was crying until she reached up and felt water on her face, but it didn’t surprise her. She would never leave Yue, not in a million years, but this was starting to hurt more than she’d bargained for.

She stayed in a tear-filled trance for what felt like hours, and was only pulled out of it by the clinking of a spoon on a glass, and a voice she despised.

“Everyone, listen up!” cried Hahn. The music stopped, and the whole crowd turned to face him. He was standing up on a table, and Yue was on the ground next to him. Even from the stairs, Katara could see Yue’s hands trembling. She was terrified. “I have some great news to tell you all! *This* lovely lady…” he pointed at Yue “is about to be granted the fortune of marrying *me* !”

The crowd burst into applause, which only made Katara feel worse. How *dare* they applaud something that was hurting so many people?

Hahn was eating it up, waving to the crowd as he jumped to the floor and threw his arm around Yue. Katara could tell that he was squeezing her tightly. “I’ll be taking congratulations at our wedding!”

Yue turned to Hahn and said something, but Katara couldn’t hear her over the noise of the crowd. “What’s that, babe?”

“I said *no* !” snapped Yue, throwing Hahn’s arm off of her. The crowd gasped, and Katara’s eyes went wide.

Yue, her hands still shaking, took a deep breath and climbed up onto the table where Hahn had been standing before turning to face him. “Hahn, I don’t *want* to marry you. I never did. I only did it because I thought I had a sense of obligation to the White Lotus. But someone very special made me realize that no obligation is worth sacrificing your own happiness.” She looked away, a twinge of guilt in her eyes. “If I’ve hurt you, I'm sorry.”

There was silence, then Hahn laughed. “She’s just joking, folks! She doesn’t know what she’s talking about!”

“Don’t know what I’m talking about?” Yue was still shaking, with anger now. “Who are you to tell me that, Hahn? What do you know about marriage? About loyalty, or being a good person? All you care about is yourself and your reputation! I don’t want any part of it.”

The crowd was hanging onto her every word.

Hahn glared at her. “What do you know about love, babe? You and me, *that’s* what love is.” He flashed a dazzling grin, but Yue didn’t smile back.

“I know a lot about love,” said Yue, getting off the table and beginning to cross the room. *She was* *coming towards the stairs* , Katara realized. “I know more than you, Hahn. I’ve been in love with that girl over there…” she pointed at Katara, and Katara felt her heart skip a beat “for a while now, and I’m not giving her up. Not for you, not for anybody else ever again.”

Yue was standing in front of Katara now, and in one smooth motion, she pulled Katara to her feet and kissed her.

Katara barely registered it, only that she thought she heard music and the crowd cheering, and *she* *was kissing Yue* , so close to her that she could hardly tell where she ended and Yue began.

They only stayed that way for a second before there was a crash on the other side of the ballroom, and all of a sudden, a knife was flying through the air towards them.

Azula’s first instinct when she saw the knives flying through the air was to run and hide. It may have been cowardly, but she knew when to attack and when to observe. Once hidden behind a pillar, she was able to survey the room. What she saw both surprised her and didn’t.

Hama, the assassin who had given Azula the very knife she was currently hiding in her pocket, was standing on top of a table in the middle of the ballroom. She had probably climbed down through the balconies, based on the fact that she had two hooks attached to her belt. Both hands were full of knives that she was throwing at every single party guest at an alarming rate. No one could cross the room to apprehend her, because the risk of being hit by a knife was too high.

Across the room, Azula spotted Aang crawling from table to table, staying close to the wall and out of Hama’s sight. That wasn’t a terrible plan. If she could stay close to the floor and out of Hama’s line of vision, she could potentially move without much risk.

The rest of the party guests, however, hadn’t had the same idea as her, or as Aang. Azula couldn’t see anything due to the enormous crowd of people running around in the center of the room, screaming their heads off (not that she blamed them.) She had no idea where her teammates were, or if they were even still alive.

Still, she began edging slowly to the left, looking for an ally in the crowd. After a minute and a half or so of carefully darting from table to table, pillar to pillar, she spotted Zuko in the crowd. Unlike the majority of the guests, her brother was running with purpose, and he was headed towards the stairs. Azula ducked her head and began to run even faster, hoping that none of Hama’s knives missed their mark and flew a little too low. She was too fond of her hair, and her life, for that to happen.

By the time Zuko reached the stairs, she was already sitting at the top of them, just out of range of Hama’s knives, twirling a strand of hair between her fingers.

“Going somewhere?”

Instead of getting mad, Zuko grabbed her hand and pulled her up the stairs, putting a finger to his lips before she could say anything else.

“What’s going on?” she whispered.

Zuko turned and glanced over the railing at the chaos down below. “Listen, I think the White Lotus is hiding something in this mansion that could be important to the case, and I think I know where it is. With everyone distracted, this might be our only chance to go and get it.” He looked up at her. “Are you ready for some secret passages?”

Azula felt a smile spreading across her face, though it was dampened by the screams coming from one floor below. “I thought you’d never ask.”

Zuko nodded, and she followed him all the way up to Pakku’s old bedroom. “What exactly are we looking for?” she asked as they walked through the doors.. “Is it worth leaving everyone down there?” she asked.

A flicker of guilt passed over Zuko’s face, but he kept walking. “There’s nothing we can do down there. We just have to hope that everything works out. But this could crack the whole case open.”

Azula’s eyes widened. “What could possibly be so groundbreaking?”

Zuko smirked as he pulled the blue rug off of the floor, revealing a locked trapdoor beneath. Instantly, Azula pulled the golden key that she and Ty Lee had found in the lounge days ago out of her pocket, sliding it into the trapdoor’s lock. The trapdoor flew open, and Zuko smiled.

“How about a box with all of the White Lotus’s deepest secrets?”

“A secret passageway in the heart of the mansion,” mused Azula. “What a development.”

Zuko grabbed a torch from the wall, and they descended into the passage. As the light from the doorway faded, Azula turned to her brother. “Do you know where this box actually is?”

“Not...exactly.”

“So we’re lost?”

“Technically, we’re not lost...yet.”

Azula sighed. “If we never get out of here, I’m blaming you.”  
“You want to solve this case just as much as I do.”

They descended another flight of stairs, and the stones around them began to turn into wood. “Look how the tunnel’s changing,” remarked Azula.

Zuko paused, his hand on one of the wooden panels. “There’s a white lotus carved into this,” he said. “We must be getting close to the center.”

“How many of these *are* there?”

Zuko shrugged. “I’m not sure. But I think they’re all over the house.”

&#46; The tunnel was slowly slanting down, and Azula could see several doorways on both sides of the passage.

“The White Lotus must have some *very* dark secrets if they built this many secret tunnels just to hide them.”

“If they’re anything like our uncle’s, I would assume so.” Zuko immediately seemed to sense that he’d said something wrong.

Azula raised an eyebrow. “Why, what’s our uncle’s secret? Did he once make a pot of tea that wasn’t perfect?”

Zuko looked away from her. If he wanted to keep this a secret, fine. Azula didn’t care about her uncle, anyway. “Something like that, yeah,” he replied.

They both lapsed into silence as they reached the very center of the passages, an octagonal room with an enormous lotus carved into each wall, and another one carved into the floor. At the center of the room, on an octagonal table, sat an octagonal box with a lotus flower carved into the top.

“The White Lotus really love their octagons, don’t they?”

Zuko smirked, though it was undermined by the worry on his face. “I guess they do.”

They reached the center, and Zuko tentatively placed his hands over the box, tracing the lotus carvings with the tips of his fingers. But he didn’t open it.

“What’s wrong?”

Zuko sighed. “This feels so...wrong. I know Uncle’s secret because he confided in me. These are secrets so deep that the White Lotus is hiding them from themselves. Do I really have a right to take them?”

Zuko’s obsession with honor and morality could occasionally prove a weakness. “Zuko, this isn’t a matter of right and wrong, this is a matter of life and death. It’s not about whether or not you have a right to those secrets. That box could hold the method for stopping many, *many* deaths, and when you have access to something so important, you need to take it. Right and wrong don’t matter anymore.”

Zuko stared at the box. Azula could see the conflict on his face.

There was a loud bang and several screams from directly above their heads.

Azula stared at Zuko. “Was that...a gunshot?”

Zuko nodded. All signs of the dilemma from just moments ago were gone from his face. “I think it was.”

Without another word, he grabbed the box, and the siblings sprinted up the stairs.

Katara’s first instinct was to leap towards Yue and knock her to the floor, and in this case, it was a lucky one, because they fell to the floor just as the knife flew over their heads. Yue grabbed Katara by the elbow and pulled her under a table. Together, they squeezed their knees into their chests and tried to get a glimpse at the chaos from under the table. It reminded Katara of the night they’d met.

Slowly and cautiously, Katara peered out from under the table. The entire party had dissolved into chaos, and at the center of it all stood Hama, the assassin who had given Katara the very ring she had on. Katara gasped, clapping her hands over her mouth.

“Do you *know* that woman?” asked Yue. Her eyes were wide, and there was a small sparkle in them that Katara was pretty sure was reflected in her own.

She nodded. “I met her earlier today, in Assassin’s Lane. She hates the White Lotus for what they did to her family.”

“Then why do you look so surprised?”

Katara sighed. Was she really *that* easy to read? “She said I reminded her of herself, and she was right. I understood her because we’ve both lost people we care about. I...I guess I just thought she was better than this.”

Yue squeezed her hand gently, and Katara felt a smile creep up her face in spite of the situation. “*You* *are* better than this. Just because she said you were similar doesn’t mean you need to give in to darkness. I know you better than that.”

“Thank you,” said Katara. Then, “Look out!” she shrieked, as a knife came flying towards the table, and the girls had to flatten themselves on the floor to avoid being pierced by its blade.

Yue smiled weakly. “I guess I won’t be using this dress anymore.” She showed Katara a tear in the hem.

“I dunno,” replied Katara, trying to ignore her rapidly beating heart. “I could see the ‘distressed clothing’ aesthetic really working for you.”

They both laughed, but Yue pulled Katara sideways before the sound could fully escape them. A knife embedded itself in the floor exactly where Katara had been sitting a moment ago. They rolled sideways, their dresses flying, their arms wrapped tightly around each other. They came to a stop under another table, their faces inches away from one another.

Before she could overthink it, Katara leaned forward and gave Yue a quick kiss before they sat up, both blushing.

Before they could do anything else, however, the tablecloth was yanked up from behind them. Katara whirled around, ready for a fight, but it was only Sokka, Aang, and Ty Lee. Sokka pressed a finger to his lips, and beckoned for Yue and Katara to follow them behind a pillar.

“Hey lovebirds, we could use your help.”

Ty Lee giggled at the nickname, but Katara just glared at her brother. “Help with *what* , exactly?”

Sokka rolled his eyes. “Aang and Ty Lee are really good at sneaking around and getting under tables without being seen. We’ve been doing our best to get as many people as we can out the door.”

All traces of irritation left Katara’s mind. “What can we do?”

Sokka stared at the four of them for a moment, contemplating. Katara wasn’t sure when or how he’d been elected the leader of this little rescue mission, but at least he wasn’t being a blockhead about it. “Right. Katara, Yue, and I are going to get as many people as we can to this pillar. After that, it’s up to you two to get them out.” He looked around. “Can everyone do that?”

Ty Lee gave him a thumbs-up. “You couldn’t ask for a better girl for the job!” She did a forward roll and disappeared under one of the tables. Katara had no idea how on Earth she managed to do forward rolls and backflips and whatever else she did in long gowns, but she seemed to be handling herself.

Aang whistled, and to Katara’s surprise, an enormous dog darted out of the crowd and over to them. Tentatively, Katara reached out and began to pet it, and the dog immediately rolled over onto its back and began wagging its tail.

Aang laughed. “This is Appa. He’s great at getting people to follow him, and he has great instincts!” He threw his arms around the dog, who licked the top of his head in response. “We’re gonna get people out of here!”

Both Aang and Appa disappeared under another table, leaving Katara, Sokka, and Yue. Seeing someone nearby, Yue dashed off into the crowd.

Sokka wiggled his eyebrows at his sister. “So...first kiss, huh?”

Katara felt her entire face heat up. “Shut up. You had yours in eighth grade during a game of Seven Minutes in Heaven.”

“That doesn’t count!” squawked Sokka indignantly. “And anyway, I wasn’t making fun of you. I’m happy for you.”

“Right, because I need your approval.” Katara rolled her eyes playfully.

“We both know you don’t. But seriously. You deserve this.” Sokka reached over and gave Katara’s arm a squeeze.

Katara smiled. “Thanks, Sokka.”

Both of them were about to head off into the crowd when a gunshot, followed by a scream, echoed through the room.

Zuko skidded back into the ballroom, just having time to shove the box into a bag, to find the entire crowd standing in a circle. Spotting Katara, Sokka, and Yue over by one side, he and Azula made their way over. “What’s going on?” he hissed.

Sokka said nothing in response, just pointed.

An old woman lay at the center of the circle, blood pouring out of her shoulder and onto the floor. She was awake and alive, but unmoving. Piandao stood over her, a gun in his hands and an absolutely furious look in his eyes that Zuko had never seen before.

“That’s Hama,” whispered Azula, fingering the hilt of her dagger. “She’s from Assassin’s Lane.”

Still holding the gun, Piandao moved closer to the fallen assassin. “I’m going to ask you once more. *What are you doing here* ?”

Hama glared up at him with venom in her eyes. “Your organization is a blight on this planet. I was only bringing you all to justice.”

“Liar!” cried Piandao, holding the gun to her head. Beside them, Yue let out a gasp. “You’re an assassin! You snuck into our mansion! I know there’s more to this than one petty revenge scheme.”

Hama let out a low laugh, and Zuko felt a ripple of shock pass through the crowd at the sound of it. “What is it you want from me, Piandao? An apology?”

“The truth,” Piandao growled.

“Fine,” spat Hama. “I despise you all. You were so obsessed with conformity and power that you *murdered* my family when we did *nothing* to you. I swore that I would not rest until I had done to you what you had done to us, and rid the Earth of your deadly presence.” She smiled, and Zuko saw that she was missing a tooth from falling when Piandao shot her. “And I *succeeded* .”

“What are you talking about?” cried Piandao. “Enough cryptic chatter, or I shoot.”

Hama laughed. “You think you’re so powerful. But I’m just a lowly little old woman from the Lower Ring, and I still managed to infiltrate one of your parties *and* kill your best friend.”

Piandao took a step back. “No…”  
“That’s right,” said Hama, still grinning her horrifying grin. “*I* murdered the head of your society. *I* murdered Pakku.”

## Chapter 26: While the Light Lasts

### Notes

#### Chapter Summary

Suki and Katara embark on a dangerous mission, while Azula and Zuko get some answers, and are confronted with even more questions.

#### Chapter Notes

TW: Weapons, fighting, mentions of torture.

Another of my favorite chapters! I really hope y'all enjoy it, so happy reading:)

### Text

Katara awoke early the next morning to find Suki standing at her front door. She could tell simply by looking at her that the other girl hadn’t slept very well. She had changed into a black tank top and camouflage-printed cargo pants since last night, but her hair had been haphazardly thrown back into a ponytail, her skin was pale, her makeup was smudged, and there were dark circles under her eyes.

Katara blinked. Despite Hama’s confession, she had slept surprisingly well. “Suki! It’s...so good to see you, um...how did you find my address?”

“The Dai Li keeps a record of everyone who lives in the city,” Suki replied somewhat coldly, brushing right past Katara despite not having been invited in. She was walking with determination and purpose, and in this state, she reminded Katara a little bit of Azula.

“Do you want some coffee, or maybe some orange juice?”

Suki waved her hand. “That’s okay. I can just borrow your coffeemaker.” She walked halfway across the kitchen before seeming to remember herself. “If that’s okay,” she added, blushing in embarrassment.

“Of course it’s okay,” Katara said hurriedly, rushing to grab a mug from her pantry. “But...uh...are you okay? You don’t seem quite...yourself.”

Suki sighed, plopping down at Katara’s counter with a cup of coffee. “I’ve thought a lot about what you said to me last night. And...I want to go get Mai back.”

Katara blinked. “Suki, I...I’m never going to stop you from helping somebody, but...it’s only been a day. Don’t you think it’s too soon? If you go on your own, they’ll be expecting you, and you won’t be able to help her at all.”

“I won’t be alone,” replied Suki, taking a sip of her coffee. “I want you to come with me.”

Katara almost dropped her coffee in surprise. “Me? But...I only sort of know how to fight. I mean, Zuko’s a detective, Ty Lee’s an acrobat, Azula carries a literal dagger in her pocket to go to the hair salon...wouldn’t it make more sense to go with someone else?”

Suki shook her head. “But *you* won’t pull me away. You understand the importance of helping the people you care about. You’re the only one I can trust to let me do this. So…” she held out her hand, “will you help me?”

Katara hesitated. She wasn’t sure she could stand by and let Suki risk her life. On the other hand, she was having a hard time standing by while Mai risked hers. She just wished no one had to get hurt, but she supposed it was already past that. So many people were dead, and she couldn’t shake the feeling that danger was lurking over all of their shoulders, waiting to strike.

But danger wasn’t going to stop her from helping her friends.

She took Suki’s hand. “Of course I will.” She paused, taking a sip of tea. It tasted mellow. “But we need some sort of weapon.”

“Let me get this straight,” said Azula. “You two are going off on what’s probably a suicide mission, you have no plan, no backup, pretty much no chance of escaping this alive, and you want to borrow my dagger?”

Katara swallowed hard. “Yeah, that’s pretty much it.” Both of them looked incredibly nervous, which was funny, in a dark sort of way.

Azula twirled a strand of hair between her fingers. “First of all, you two need to stop trembling like leaves. If you can’t come over here to ask me for my dagger, then don’t even bother sneaking back into Lake Laogai. You’ll be eaten alive.”

“Thanks for the pep talk,” Suki said dryly.

“Look, if you wanted a pep talk, you should have gone somewhere else. Go ask Ty Lee. You came *here* looking for weapons.” Azula pulled the dagger out of her topknot, where she’d been trying to keep it since last night. It worked surprisingly well, probably because she made her topknots so goddamn *tight* . “And I think I have what you’re looking for.”

“You keep your dagger in your *hair* ?!” cried Katara.

“Don’t sound so surprised, *look* at my fingernails. Do you know anyone else who has fingernails this sharp?” She pointed at Suki. “That one carries fans that could kill you in an instant. I don’t see the difference.”

“Never mind,” sighed Katara. “Can we have the dagger or not?”

Azula sighed. Since receiving it, the dagger had become rather dear to her. She would prefer it if her friends didn’t lose it on some insane rescue mission. On the other hand, they were her friends, and though she didn’t have the widest range of knowledge on the subject, she felt fairly certain that giving friends your possessions was something people did from time to time. “Why don’t you want me to come with you? The more people, the higher a chance you have of not getting yourselves killed, right?”

Suki looked guiltily at the floor. “Look, Azula, it’s not that you’re not really smart and talented, but...I don’t think you’re right for this.”

“Because?”

Suki looked away. Azula rolled her eyes. “I won’t be offended. I’m a perfectionist, remember? If something about me is not the very best that it should be, it needs to be fixed, and if I am to fix it, I need to know what it is. So spit it out.”

Suki sighed. “It’s just...the last time we went to Lake Laogai, you’re the one who stopped me from running after Mai.”

“That was to ensure that you didn’t get yourself captured or killed, thus rendering Mai’s sacrifice useless.”

“I know,” said Suki. “But this...I know you’re pragmatic, and you don’t love risks when you don’t think they’ll play out in your favor. But this *is* a risk. It doesn’t make sense, and maybe we won’t come back, and I know that, but I have to do it anyway, and I need someone who won’t try and stop me.” She looked up, her blue eyes wide. “Does that make sense?”

Azula pondered for a moment. Her friends were idiots to try this at all, but perhaps they were right about this. Maybe she *would* try and stop them.

She sighed. She didn’t like the idea of losing them to this insane mission, but she knew that they were going, with or without her support.

So she tossed them the dagger. “I think you need this more than I do,” she said as she redid her topknot. Pulling the knife out had loosened a couple of strands.

Katara’s eyes widened, and Suki caught the dagger in her hands with a small smile.“Really?” asked Katara.

Azula nodded. “Don’t get yourselves killed and then never bring it back, because then I’ll have to come to Lake Laogai and kill you a second time myself.” She smirked at them, getting to her feet. “I need to go. Zuko and I are trying to interrogate Hama. But, a word of advice.” She turned in the doorway to face the two girls, possibly for the last time ever. “Don’t go before dark unless you *really* have a death wish.”

Zuko stared at the assassin sitting across from him. He and Azula had been asking her questions for an hour, but she had refused to say anything. He hated interrogations like this. They usually led somewhere eventually, but Zuko hated waiting for them to get there. He was more of an ‘instant results’ kind of person.

Next to him, Azula was examining her nails, an interrogation technique that Zuko had seen her use more than once. It was certainly chilling, but Zuko did wonder why she wasn’t using her dagger. Ever since she’d gotten her hands on it, he hadn’t seen her pass up a chance to use it even once.

Apparently, Hama had the same idea. In a flash, she reached across the table and grabbed Azula’s wrist, and though Zuko could see that she wasn’t gripping very tightly, Azula didn’t pry off her hand. “Where’s your dagger, Firecracker?” she taunted the girl. “Were you not strong enough to use it? I had such high hopes for you.”

Zuko half expected his sister to pull out the dagger and stab the assassin through the neck right then and there, but instead she looked her coldly in the eyes. She didn’t even blink. “It’s absolutely none of your business what I did with my dagger. You gave it to me, and therefore it *doesn’t* *belong to you* .” She pulled her hand away.

Hama laughed. “And my information *doesn’t belong to you* , Detectives. So I suggest you stop trying to get it.”

“On the contrary,” interjected Zuko. “This information belongs to us because it concerns the city we live in, the places we go, and the people we love. We have been tangled up in this mystery since the beginning, and we have the right to know absolutely everything about it.” He leaned forward. “And let me remind you which of us has the power here. Just to be *one hundred percent* *clear.* ”

“Impressive,” murmured Azula. Zuko rolled his eyes. Every time he forgot how condescending she could be, she reminded him.”

Hama laughed. “You think your empty threats will work on me? I know you don’t have the guts for anything real.”

“I don’t care what I have the *guts* for,” hissed Zuko. “I’m getting very tired of working on this case, and I, for one, would like it if everyone in this city stopped dying. So either you give us answers and a reason to keep interrogating you, or we leave, and you don’t have anyone to taunt or talk to anymore.”

“Or,” added Azula, “someone to brag about your exploits to. If we leave now, some of your handiwork might go uncredited. Is that what you really want?”

“You’ve already killed one person,” said Zuko. “You have nothing to lose.”

Hama smirked at them. “I don’t think you two realize how similar you are to me.”

“Believe me,” said Azula. “We know.”

“Well then,” said Hama, leaning back in her chair, “you should have already deduced that it was me who killed Professor Zei.”

Zuko’s eyes widened. “How?”

“Isn’t it obvious?” laughed Hama. “Slow-acting poison. Works like a charm every time.”

“So you’re well-versed in the art of knife-throwing *and* poisions,” mused Azula. “Impressive. Somebody must have paid a *very* large sum of money to hire you.”

“As a matter of fact,” said Hama, leaning back in her chair, “someone did. But if you want to know who, you’re out of luck. The person who hired me could do *far* worse to me than prison.”

Zuko leaned forward. “Was it the Dai Li?” he asked. “We know what they do. If you confess, we can protect you.”

Hama glared at him. “I don’t need your protection,” she spat. “For your information, I’m quite enjoying this little string of death we have going. Everyone in the White Lotus *and* the Dai Li deserves it.”

“Did you commit the other murders?” asked Zuko.

Hama shook her head. “I wish I could take credit, but no. The person who hired me was better at covering their tracks than that.”

As the sun was setting, Katara and Suki stood behind an unusually large birch tree, directly next to the entrance to Lake Laogai. In keeping with Azula’s advice, they hadn’t gone into the woods until the sun started to dip low in the sky.

“Here’s the plan,” hissed Suki, as they heard the first crickets of the night begin to call.

“There’s a plan?” whispered Katara.

Suki glared at her. “Of course there’s a plan! I wasn’t going to go in on a rescue mission without a plan! Who do you take me for?”

“Got it, got it,” murmured Katara hurriedly. “Sorry.”

“Here’s the plan,” Suki said again. “We’ve seen guards going in and out for the past...however long we’ve been here. The next time some guards come by, we’re going to knock them out and steal their uniforms.”

“There are *a lot* of things about what you just said that I don’t like.”

“Like what?”

“Like leaving two poor random guards out in the October cold without clothes!”

Suki stared at her. “Katara, these could be the same people that are torturing our friend. Do you really think they deserve our sympathy?” Suki was normally a sympathetic person, but Mai was in danger, maybe hurt, maybe even worse, because of her, and she was going to stop at *nothing* to get her back.

“Right,” muttered Katara. “You’re right.”

“So, what else don’t you like about the plan?”

Katara toyed nervously with her fingers. “I’m...not sure I can knock people out. I’ve had a few combat lessons, but that’s nothing compared to you.”

“Nonsense.” Suki took her friend’s hands. “Katara, I asked for you to be here because I knew you could do this. All it takes to become a great fighter is hard work and a little faith. You’re more than capable.” She may have been desperate, but Suki meant every word of it. “You’re stronger than you think, you know.” She spotted two guards walking towards the entrance. “Now, go!”

She leaped out from behind the tree and tackled the first guard to the ground, holding her fan to his throat. “Stay perfectly still,” she hissed. The guard went limp beneath her. “Good,” she said matter-of-factly. “I’m sorry for what I’m about to do.”

She grabbed a tree branch and whacked the guard over the head, hoping she hit hard enough but not too hard. The guard collapsed to the ground, unconscious but alive.

Suki was getting up when the second guard ran up and grabbed her by the waist, lifting her into the air. Before she could react, though, the arms were releasing her. She turned and saw Katara standing over the second guard’s unconscious body, another tree branch in her hands. She gave Suki a small smile. “Looks like I did it.”

Suki smiled back. “Yeah, looks like you did.”

Suki’s uniform was significantly too big on her, and she had to roll up both the sleeves and the legs about six times before they were short enough for running and fighting. In contrast, Katara’s was too short, and only came about halfway down her lower legs.

“Should we switch?” asked Katara. “Wouldn’t that make more sense? I’m taller than you.”

Suki checked her watch. True night was only just falling over the forest, but their time was limited. “We don’t have time. We need to go now!”

Thankfully, Katara didn’t ask any more questions, and the two girls descended into the tree trunk, trying their best to look like they belonged there.

“Hey!” shouted a guard almost as soon as they got in. “There’s the last two! Where were you?”

“We got lost,” Suki said quickly, hoping that they would buy it. “First time out here.”

“Ah!” laughed the guard, who, upon closer inspection, looked like she was some sort of captain. “That happens to everyone. Well, time to get you two with your groups! Now, you go this way, and you with the auburn hair can follow me.”

Katara shot Suki a panicked glance, but Suki didn’t let her fear show. Any wrong move could cost them both their lives. “Wait!” she cried, trying as hard as she could to piece her thoughts together in time. “We actually need to stay together, because…” she tried hard to think of something “because Long Feng ordered it! He saw us together in training, and he said we made an impeccable team.” Suki knew that, in the Dai Li, Long Feng’s word was law. There was no way the captain could refuse that.

Sure enough, she didn’t. “Right! Then you two can go right to the science sector.” She pointed to the center corridor. “Right down that one there. Good luck,” she added wryly before heading off to the right.

With no other choice, the two girls headed down the center corridor. Once they were alone, Katara leaned in and whispered into Suki’s ear. “What are we going to do?”

“Don’t worry,” replied Suki. “The second we know t where Mai is, we’ll go find her. We just need to listen to the other guards.”  
“And hope for the best?”  
“You’re usually pretty hopeful! Think you can hold out hope a little longer?” Suki didn’t mean it as a joke, but Katara laughed anyway.

“Probably,” she said. “But this has to be the worst plan I’ve ever heard of.”

“Some things are more important than plans,” Suki muttered to herself, gripping one of her fans under her sleeve. Katara nodded in agreement as they rounded the next corner, right before they ran smack into another pair of guards.

“New recruits!” chirped the first. “Are you having a good first day?”

“Yes!” replied Katara with a little too much enthusiasm. “We’re having a perfect first day!”

“Wonderful!” cried the first one. “I love meeting new recruits! It’s so exciting!” He leaned in closer. “So you’ve been assigned to the science sector, right?”

“That’s right,” chimed in Suki. “You, too?”

The two guards looked at each other and giggled. “We are,” began the second, leaning in, “but we’re sneaking off to the prison sector right now.”

“Oh?” asked Suki, trying to keep her cool, despite that every part of her was screaming that *this* *was important!* “And why is that?”

“Oh, that’s right,” said the first guard. “I forgot; you’re new, so of course you wouldn’t know about this.” He leaned in closer, dropping his voice to a whisper. “They brought in a new prisoner a couple of nights ago. Apparently, she was one of us, but betrayed us. Young, too. They’re planning a big, public thing for her with the Master of Pain. To make an example out of her.”

“And you’re *okay* with this?” cried Katara.

The guards shrugged. “It is kind of sad,” said the second, “what with her being young and all. But...it’s the only thing that’s *happened* around here for ages. We want to see it.”

“Mmmhmm,” said Suki. “When did you say this was?”

“I dunno,” said the first guard. “In about half an hour, maybe.”

The girls exchanged a glance. “Well, would you look at that!” cried Katara. “Looks like we’ve got to get to our next post! We really should be going! Nice meeting you, though!” Suki grabbed her wrist and the girls set off down the hallway.

The second the other guards were out of sight, they began to sprint. As they raced down the stone hallways, Suki could feel her heartbeat growing faster and faster. Thinking of Mai in danger, about to be potentially tortured, made her absolutely furious, possibly more so than she had ever been in her life. Thinking of seeing Mai again made her chest feel a little like there was some sort of light inside, making her tickle. Wanting to protect Mai filled her with a deep determination that possessed every inch of her body. She sprinted faster.

At last, the shelves of potions and experiments gave way to stone walls and prison bars. Suki began running frantically from cell to cell, checking every single door, even shaking the bars in desperation. She could feel her panic begin to rise as time continued to run out.

“Suki!” cried Katara from somewhere down the tunnel. “We need to split up, or we’ll never get to all of these in time!”

Suki paused for a fraction of a second, turning to face her friend. “Are you okay with that?”

Katara swallowed nervously, but nodded. Suki gave her a quick hug before turning and running in the opposite direction. She could hear the sounds of a crowd moving towards her, and she began running in the same direction they were going, doing her best to stay out of sight.

She came to a screeching halt as she came to the head of a hallway filled with guards, all filing towards a round room up ahead, probably where the demonstration was going to take place. Mai was probably somewhere on the other side of that room, if she could only get past the guards…

There was no time to overthink things, only time for action. Suki took a deep breath, pulled out one of her fans, and began to sprint through the crowd, ducking and rolling and dodging and slicing to the best of her ability. She felt a few muscles twist in her legs, and it wasn’t perfect, but she kept moving, ignoring the shouts of the guards around her. Along the way, she grabbed a key out of one of the guard’s pockets, hoping it was the key she needed. If she could just move fast enough, she could do this, especially if she kept the element of surprise on her side.

Breaking free of the crowd and ignoring the pain in her legs, Suki gathered up all of her strength and sprinted through the round room, ignoring the shouts of the guards around her. She didn’t pause to choose a doorway, she just sprinted straight ahead, praying that it was the right one. As she sprinted up the hallway, she yanked a chain, pulling down a door between her and the guards. At least that would buy her a few minutes, even if they were a short few minutes.

She ran from cell to cell as fast as she could, ignoring her shortness of breath, ignoring every pain in her body, until she found her.

Mai was sitting towards the back of her cell, her legs bunched up, staring into space with an expression of extreme boredom. When she saw Suki, she looked up.

“Are you here to torture me already? You’re early.”

It was only then that Suki realized that, with her hair in a sloppy ponytail, dark clothing, and two streaks of black paint on her face, she didn’t look much like herself. She leaned closer to the bars, trying to make herself as visible as possible. “Mai...it’s me.”

Mai’s eyes widened, and in a flash, she was directly across from Suki, gripping her wrists. “Suki, don’t be stupid. I’m here so you don’t have to be. Why would you waste that?”

Well, it was now or never. Why was this scarier than breaking into the Dai Li’s fortress?

Slowly, she slid her hands down so that they were intertwined with Mai’s. Even in the darkness, Suki saw two spots of color appear on Mai’s face, and even without a mirror, she knew she wore matching ones on her own.

“Because I couldn’t stand to leave you here. Life was…” she gave Mai a small smile “boring without you.”

And without another thought, she leaned through the bars and kissed her.

She felt Mai’s face tense up in surprise, but it quickly faded as Mai leaned even further into the kiss, pulling Suki as close as she possibly could.

They broke apart, both blushing hard, both smiling. Only the sounds of shouts down the hall reminded Suki that they were still at Lake Laogai.

She turned back to Mai, all business again. “We need to get you out of here!”

“Well, if I could do that, I’d have done it already.” Mai rolled her eyes, but she was still smiling. “You don’t know how to pick locks, do you?”

“No,” sighed Suki, “but I can use this.” She pulled out the key she’d stolen from the guard and turned it in the lock.

The cell door opened, and Mai walked out tentatively, almost as if she couldn’t believe that her experience was real. Suki threw her arms around her and hugged her tightly, ignoring Mai’s halfhearted cries of protest. She could hear Mai’s laughter through her pretend grumbles.

“Guys!” came a cry from further up the hallway. “You’re okay!”

They turned and saw Katara standing at the end of the hallway. Both of her shoes were off, and she was holding them in her hands. It looked as though she was using them as weapons. She glanced back at a hallway behind her that Suki couldn’t see. “I’m sure you’re having a nice reunion, but we need to get out of here now!”

Neither girl said another word, but they did clasp hands as they sprinted down the hallway towards Katara. They reached their friend just as Suki’s door broke, and another army of guards came at them from the left.

“Time to hit the road!” yelled Mai. She grabbed a fan out of Suki’s pocket and threw it at the crowd. Even with a weapon that wasn’t her own, her aim was true.

Using the last of their strength, the three girls sprinted up the stairs and out of the fortress. Once in the forest, Mai indicated a tree with wide, plentiful branches, and the three girls quickly climbed up, cloaking themselves in the darkness, out of sight of the Dai LI.

Suki squeezed Mai’s hand even more tightly, and Mai leaned into Suki’s shoulder. “I missed you,” Suki murmured.

Mai smirked. “You too, Princess.”

The moment was interrupted by a phone call from Zuko on Katara’s cell phone. The faces of Sokka, Zuko, and Azula stared back at them through the screen, but Katara put her finger to her lips before any of them could speak. “We’re hiding from the Dai Li,” hissed Katara. “We’re all fine, but be quiet.”

All three of them nodded.

“What’s going on?” whispered Suki, leaning closer to the phone.

Zuko looked away guiltily from the camera. “Well, we looked into the White Lotus’s secret box.”

“And?”

“They truly have many secrets,” said Azula. “It’s quite remarkable. Bumi stole money to pursue wrestling, Uncle was a vigilante of all things, Jeong Jeong trained the Master of Pain…”

“Azula!” Sokka hissed. “Not the point!”

“What’s the point?” scoffed Mai. “They’re all shady? We got that.”

“It’s not that,” said Zuko, still refusing to look at the camera. “It’s...it’s about Yon Rha.”

“The super old one?” asked Suki. “What about him?”

Zuko’s whole face seemed to be made of guilt as he spoke. “I...have some news about Yon Rha. And you’re not going to like it.”

“Well, spit it out then!” snapped Katara. “Get it over with!”

Zuko looked directly at the camera for the first time. His eyes conveyed his message clearly: *I’m* *sorry.*

“Katara...Yon Rha killed your mother.”

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes
