## Chapter 33: The Red Signal

### Notes

#### Chapter Summary

After a fight gone wrong and the appearance of a new threat, Azula is forced to grapple with the past and the present.

#### Chapter Notes

TW: Guns, knives, panic attacks, mild flashbacks, physical threats, descriptions of physical combat.

Sorry this one's a little late for posting, but it's one of my favorites! Definitely one of my top 5 for the whole fic! You'll see why when you get to the end ( no skipping ahead!)

Happy reading:)

### Text

Only seconds later, the police swarmed around them, accompanied by the Mayor. Zuko stood up to talk to them.

“Thank you for coming, Mr. Mayor,” he said. “The rest of the Dai Li agents should be in the cells downstairs.”

“Ooh, you locked them in?” chirped Kuei. “Very clever!” He clapped excitedly, then, seeming to remember what was actually going on, his expression turned serious and his voice grew quiet as he caught sight of Zhao’s body. “Oh my. What happened here?”

Azula had dropped to the floor, staring at the bloody dagger in her hands in shock. “I’m not sure.” She spoke in a complete monotone, devoid of any emotion or conviction. “We were fighting, and he swung his sword at me…” she gestured to a sword lying on the floor twenty feet or so below the ledge “so I swung my dagger, and I cut him in the shoulder. It wasn’t a big cut, not big enough to kill, but then...he died.” She got up and looked the Mayor in the eyes. Zuko didn’t think he’d ever seen her this surprised before. “Sokka says he thinks the blade was poisoned, but I promise, if the blade was poisoned, I had absolutely no idea.”

The Mayor turned to Sokka. “Are you qualified to tell her that the blade was poisoned?”

Sokka swallowed nervously, but nodded. “I’m a forensics student, Mr. Mayor. I can’t be certain...we’d need to do more tests for that, but...this isn’t the first time I’ve seen a case like this. Someone was accidentally injected with an incredibly high dose of botulinum toxin A. They died nearly instantly.”

“What is botulinum toxin A?”

“It’s one of the most toxic substances on the planet. Look at him.” Sokka gestured towards Zhao. “He’s paralyzed. That’s a clear symptom.”

“Am *I* poisoned?” asked Azula, holding her dagger out at arm’s length.

“If it’s only on the blade of your dagger, no. We’ll need to do more tests to confirm this, but…”

The Mayor nodded. “The evidence does seem rather overwhelming.”

One of the policemen came up behind Azula and grabbed her wrists. Startled, she tried to run away, but he held her tightly and didn’t let go. Her pupils seemed to dilate right before Zuko’s eyes, and she began to breathe shallowly and quickly.

“What are you doing?” snapped Zuko. “She didn’t do anything wrong!”

Kuei sighed. “There’s just some red tape we need to get around. If she truly didn’t know the dagger was poisoned, there’s nothing to worry about.” He gestured to one of the police next to him, who picked Azula’s dagger up off the ground and placed it into a ziplock bag. “Take this to the labs and analyze it as fast as you can.”

“Heat it to 85 degrees celsius to get the poison off when you’re done!” yelled Sokka as the guards left.

The Mayor turned to Azula with a sad expression on his face. “Until we figure this out, I’m sorry to say this, but you’re under arrest for Zhao’s murder.”

At least the officer sitting across from her in the office was kind. Azula wasn’t usually much for kindness, but today, she needed it more than ever.

She had felt so *powerful* when she was running on nothing but adrenaline, anger, and a desire to avenge herself. She had wanted Zhao dead, but in the wake of his death, which had come by her hand but *still* not by her choice, all of the adrenaline drained out of her. She still felt so *powerless* .

First, she’d been tortured into revealing her greatest fear, and then, just when she’d thought she was finding herself and fixing her problems, her own dagger had been poisoned without her knowledge, and she’d been tricked into committing murder.

She felt like a puppet on strings, as though she had no control over her life at all. The exact feeling she’d been trying to avoid when she’d come to Ba Sing Se.

She was finally building a life for herself, but she’d never felt so out-of-control before. It was absolutely terrifying.

“Ma’am?” said the officer’s gentle voice from the other side of the desk. “I just need you to answer a few questions for me. Can you do that?”

*We ask the questions here.* Zhao’s voice rippled through her mind, and all of a sudden, the handcuffs around her hands became ropes, and she was back in that dark cell again, knives cutting into her skin, malicious laughter echoing all around her, with no escape, no hope, no power…

“Ma’am?”

Azula blinked. No, she wasn’t back there again. She had fought Zhao and she had won. They had no power over her any more. She was inside a police interrogation room because of some red tape. That was all.

“Sorry,” she said, feeling the fear in her own voice. “What was the question?”

The young officer smiled sympathetically at her. “No need to apologize. If I understand correctly, what happened to you was rather...traumatic. Take all the time you need.”

Well, *that* was something she’d never heard before.

Azula nodded. “Just ask the question.” After a moment, she added a rather awkward “please.”

“All right,” said the officer. “I was asking if you could please give me a little run-down of your fight with Zhao. From start to finish.”

“I can try,” said Azula, trying to stop the images of the dark cell and the knives and the syringe with the blue drug from creeping into her brain, even though they were flashing before her eyes every time she blinked. “Let’s see...my friends and I were searching for prisoners in the secret passages under the Dai Li mansion, and…”

“How did you know the prisoners would be there?”

It struck Azula as a bit of an odd question, but she couldn’t let her mind linger on it. She was too eager to *just get the hell out of that office.* “We’re detectives. We weren’t sure that the prisoners would be there, but we inferred it based on previous evidence.”

The officer nodded, writing something down in her notebook. “Please continue.”

“Right,” said Azula. “We found the prisoners, but Zhao and his guards apprehended us. From there, we split up to try and fight them off, and I ran after Zhao…”

“Any particular reason why?”

Azula sighed. She had known this was going to come up, but it didn’t make it any easier. “Zhao...Zhao is also known as the Master of Pain, because he carries out physical torture for the Dai Li. Last night, he and Long Feng decided to test out their methods on a new victim.”

*I believe you are already acquainted with the Master of Pain?* Long Feng’s voice echoed through the room, and she wanted to pull her hands up and cover her ears like a small child, but all she could do was rattle her bruised wrists against her handcuffs.

“Azula?”

Azula blinked. There were no other voices in the room. No one was going to ruin her body, and nobody was going to turn her own mind against her. She was safe. So why did she still feel like someone was shoving her through death’s door?

“Sorry, can you repeat that?”

“I said, who was the victim?”

The moment of truth. Azula sighed, unable to meet the officer’s eyes. “Me.”

*Oh, Little Charmer, I suppose you should learn to be more alert while you sleep.*

The officer made another note in their notebook, and nodded at Azula to continue.

“The memory becomes rather blurry once we started fighting, I’m afraid. We came into a round, stone room with a ledge encircling the wall about nineteen or twenty feet above the ground.”

“How did one get up to this ledge?”

“There were two flights of stairs, one on either side of the door. Anyway, once I chased him into the room, we fought on the ground for a while, and then he raced up to the ledge and threw something at me.” Azula twitched her shoulder in the direction of the officer. There was still blood on her sweater. “I chased him up onto the ledge, and held him at knifepoint for a while, and then he swung his sword and I swung my dagger, and I sliced through his shoulder, and the next thing I knew…” she looked the officer right in the eyes, “he was dead.”

The officer was taking more notes in their notebook when there was a knock at the door. A moment later, Zuko entered and took a seat in the chair next to Azula. She looked at him in surprise, but he offered her a small smile.

Y *ou’ll never have what I have. Not someone like you.*

No, no, no! That was a nightmare caused by the Dai Li and their twisted tricks. They’d all been apprehended now. It wasn’t real.

*You see, we are very close to making that nightmare a reality, if we so desire.*

But they couldn’t. They had no power over her.

*She was back in the dark room already. She could never escape. They had taken away her power,* *and she could never get it back.*

But she’d *gotten* it back.

“Welcome, Detective,” said the officer, bringing Azula’s mind back to Earth. “I just have a few more questions for your sister, we need to wait on the test results, and you should be free to go.”

“What test results?” the siblings asked at the same time.  
“Apparently, the poison on your dagger leaves traces,” said the officer. “We took a sample off of you back under the Dai Li mansion. If you have no traces of botulinum toxin A on you, that should help your case.”

Azula should have felt relieved, but all she felt was more fear. She could feel her breath quickening, as the air in the room became thicker.

“Azula?” Zuko’s voice pierced through the haze. “Are you all right?”  
“Of course,” she managed to say. Soon, this would all be over. “Please, continue with your questions.”

“Right,” said the officer. “You said that you fought Zhao on the floor and then up on the ledge. Can you tell me who had the upper hand in this fight the whole time?”

“Well,” said Azula, “I suppose it was me.”

“If you don’t mind my asking, why didn’t you just kill him?

*You lie.*

It was as though Long Feng and Zhao were standing right in front of her, prying through her mind, analyzing each and every word she said, nothing ever enough to stop them from hurting her again and again and again. She could practically feel the blade of Zhao’s ring cutting through her face.

“Well, it wasn’t enough of an upper hand to kill him instantly. He put up a fight.”

“And when you held him at knifepoint over the edge? Why didn’t you kill him then?”

*Insolent girl!*

Their faces were getting closer and closer to her, and Azula could have sworn that the handcuffs were tightening around her wrists, like ropes.

Azula took a deep breath. “I...suppose I was angry at him. After he tortured me, I feel... *felt* like he had taken away my power, used me, made me weak. I wanted to get my power back, and make him experience the same things he’d done to me.”

“What exactly did he *do* to you?”

“Is this relevant?” snapped Zuko from his chair.

“ *Very* relevant, Detective,” replied the officer with a sad smile.

“It’s all right, Zuko,” said Azula, even though it *wasn’t* all right, and every time she described an aspect of that night, she felt like she was experiencing it all over again; the knives, the bruising, the taunting, the fear. “Zhao and Long Feng wanted information they thought I had. When I didn’t give it to them, they resorted to cutting, punching, basically inflicting every surface wound possible without rendering me unconscious. When that didn’t work…” She was panting now, and she could see Long Feng raising the syringe, ready to stab it through her arm. “They tried injecting me with one of their experimental drugs. It makes you hallucinate, and I *hated* having my own mind turned against me. More than anything.” She was having a hard time breathing now, as the hazy image of Long Feng raised the syringe and plunged it through her skin, her left arm exploding with pain.

“I see,” said the officer in a cold, clipped tone that mirrored Long Feng’s so much that Azula felt tears in the corners of her eyes. They really *had* stolen her power. “Might your anger have taken you to a...dark place? Dark enough to poison your blade?”

*You may do the honors. This little brat has yet to experience true pain. I trust that you can fix that.*

They were going to come for her again, Azula was sure of it. She was tied to her chair and there was nothing she could do about it.

She began thrashing against her handcuffs, trying desperately to escape the dark room that was closing in around her, but the metal only slammed into her skin, leaving bruises even darker than her eyes.

“Please!” yelled the officer, “Try to restrain yourself!”

“Shut up, you fucking moron!” yelled Zuko. “Can’t you see she’s panicking? Let her out of that chair!”

“I’m not technically allowed to…”

“I don’t give a flying fuck about your rules. Let my sister out of that chair, or else we’re not answering any more questions from you or your colleagues. I was at that fight. I know Azula stabbed Zhao in self defense. That alone is enough to bypass all of your stupid questions.”

Azula’s breathing was becoming so shallow that the room was spinning, and the handcuffs felt so tight around her wrists that she thought her hands might fall off.

The second the officer unlocked the handcuffs, Azula sprinted out of the interrogation room as fast as she possibly could. She didn’t stop until she found the brightest corner of the police station, all the way up in its attic, next to a window. There she leaned against the wall, where no one could sneak up from behind her, curled her knees into a ball, buried her face in her hands, and tried to remember how to breathe.

Zuko found his sister sitting in an empty room on the third floor. She seemed calmer than before, though there were still tear tracks on her face.

He sat down next to her, trying not to startle her. “You okay?”  
She shook her head, sighing. “I thought re-entering the investigation would help me regain my sense of control. But it just made it worse. The entire time I was in there, I kept feeling like I was back in *that place* all over again. I want to move on, but I keep reliving it whenever I get reminded of it.” She sighed, slumping against the wall. “Why is this so hard?”

“I know what you mean,” said Zuko. “I went through the same thing after I got this.” He gestured towards the scar on his face.

Azula’s eyes widened. “How did you get through it?” It was weird seeing her so open, so desperate. Zuko couldn’t decide if he liked having her be so honest with him or hated how shaken she seemed.

“I’m not really sure,” replied Zuko. “I tried to shut myself off from the world to avoid anyone who could hurt me like Father did. I thought it would help, but I think it just made me more scared, in the end.” He sighed. “Honestly, it helped me the most to know that I could protect myself from something like that ever happening again. I found my own strength, in some sort of way.”

“But that’s the problem,” said Azula. “I *had* strength, and it feels like they took it away. They made me so weak, I…” she turned to him, more tears streaming down her cheeks. The effect was alarming. “I don’t know if I can ever get it back.”

“But you never lost it,” replied Zuko. “Just because you’ve been through something like this doesn’t make you any less powerful. Look at you! You survived! It’s only been a day, and you’ve already faced the man who tortured you in a fight and come out on top!”

“But I didn’t have any power over that fight, either!”

“Yes, you did! You didn’t know your blade was poisoned, sure, but the rest of the fight? The part where you kicked Zhao’s sorry ass? That was you.”

A small smile crossed Azula’s face. “You really think so.”

“Unquestionably.”

She sighed, staring up at the ceiling. “Who knew you were so good at pep talks?”

“You would have, if you ever asked.”

They both laughed, but were interrupted by a knock. Azula froze, her entire body on high alert. “Come in!” called Zuko.

The officer from the interrogation poked their head through the door. “The lab results came back negative.” They tossed Azula the ziplock bag with her dagger in it. “Poison’s been removed. You can have this back, and you’re free to go.” They looked rather sheepishly at the ground. “And, for what it’s worth, I’m sorry about that. I didn’t mean to scare you. I’m just...new at this job.”

“No worries,” said Zuko, and Azula nodded, already running her fingers over the flat edge of her dagger. It fit so perfectly in her hands, it was almost scary.

As the officer left, Zuko’s phone pinged with a text from Mai. *Suki and I talked to the police,* it read. *You can thank us later.*

Zuko showed Azula the text, and she laughed. “Maybe I will thank them later,” she murmured.

Another call came in on Zuko’s phone just as the siblings were getting up to leave, and Zuko frowned at the caller. He clicked *reply* , and Yue’s worried-looking face popped up on his screen.

“Yue?” said Azula, sounding as surprised as Zuko felt. Not that Yue wasn’t Zuko’s friend, but if she needed someone, she almost always asked for Katara. “Is something wrong?”

“I’m not sure,” whispered Yue. “Maybe.” As she leaned in closer to the camera, Zuko noticed that she was wearing what appeared to be a blue, sequined dress. The White Lotus must have been in the middle of yet another party. “I saw someone I didn’t recognize in the garden earlier tonight. We’re having a party, so I didn’t think too much of it, but...this guy was acting weird. Muttering something about *White Lotus scum* and *girls who pretended to be innocent* and *last chances.* I thought you might know something about it.”

Considering how pale Azula’s face had just gotten, Zuko would wager that she did indeed know something. “Did you catch this person’s name?”

Yue nodded. “I overheard him talking to someone on the phone,” she replied. “I think he said his name was Jet.”

Azula stood up abruptly, looking panicked, her eyes gleaming with determination. “We’re going to the White Lotus mansion. *Now* .”

“Hang on a minute,” said Zuko. “Can I at least get an explanation for this?”  
Azula shook her head. “I’m sorry, but there’s no time.” She was already running out the door.

“Wait!” cried Yue over the phone. “This is an exclusive party! There’s no way you’ll be let into the mansion without some sort of formal wear!”

“Not a problem,” said Azula, and she reached over and hung up the phone before sprinting at full speed out the door. Zuko followed her into the dark streets, towards the train station for the Upper Ring.

They stopped in front of a clothing store, which was closed since it was so late at night, but the light was on. “Five-second explanation,” snapped Zuko irritably. “That’s all I want.”

“Fine,” said Azula as she banged on the door. She still looked panicked. “If I’m right, Ty Lee is in a lot of danger right now. Last time she met Jet, he called her White Lotus scum and they talked about innocence. Seems to match up freakishly perfectly with what Yue said, doesn’t it?”

Zuko felt a shiver go down his spine. “If that’s true, then…”

“Then we can’t afford to wait any longer.” Azula reached up and smashed the glass on the store window, causing the startled store owner to race to the front of the shop.

“Don’t move or I’ll shoot!” He held up a gun.

Zuko stepped in. “Look, Mister, we’re having an emergency. There could be lives at stake.”

“Important lives,” added Azula

“If we could just have one piece of formal something for her…”

“Are you insane?” cried the man. “I’m calling the police!”

“So much for being polite,” grumbled Azula, pulling out her dagger and pointing it at the man’s throat. “All right, Mister. We aren’t robbing you. Either you give us a piece of formalwear right now, and we will pay for it, or I shove the tip of this knife through your neck. Which would you prefer?” She pressed it closer. “Did I mention we’re in a time crunch?”

“Right this way!” squawked the man, and they disappeared into the shop.

Fire minutes later, Azula emerged and began sprinting again. Luckily for her, the deep red tuxedo she had bought in a hurry fit her like a glove, and was ideal for running. Its hems were already damp from the puddles on the street from the recent rains, but she didn’t care.

She could sense Zuko following her, but she tuned out the sound of his footsteps. She could only think of Ty Lee.

She was perfect, and Azula didn’t say that lightly. She exuded happiness, beauty, and *love* . She was someone special, and Azula had been letting her go.

Well, she wasn’t going to let Jet hurt her. If she couldn’t love Ty Lee the way she wanted, the way Ty Lee deserved, she could at least keep her safe. She wasn’t sure she would be able to cope with the gaping hole that would inevitably drill itself into her heart if Ty Lee were to be hurt, or worse.

She sprinted down street after street, alleyway after alleyway, until, after what seemed like an eternity of sprinting, she arrived at the White Lotus mansion.

“You look awfully roughed-up to be coming to a party,” said the guard at the gate.

Azula glared at him with every ounce of passion and malice in her body. “Just let me in.”

The guard let her in, and she raced up towards the mansion and across the lawn. Just as she was about to enter the ballroom, she heard a scream from the balcony on the top floor. A *familiar* scream.

She was the only person outside, and she was sure nobody else had heard it.

It was down to her, and no one else. And she refused to let this world lose someone so perfect.

Azula had never run as fast as she ran up the spiral staircases in the mansion, leaping over two steps at a time, then four, then six. When she got to the top, she was so full of adrenaline and determination that she didn’t even stop to catch her breath. She sprinted through the nearest bedroom, and came skidding out onto the balcony, dagger in hand, her suit jacket flapping in the wind.

Jet stood in front of her, restraining a trembling Ty Lee by the back of her multicolored dress, and holding a gun to her head.

Seeing Ty Lee so terrified, seeing someone *threaten* her, unlocked something like fire inside Azula. It was like what she’d experienced fighting Zhao, but in addition to the fury, there was a deep desire to protect.

“Drop that gun.” Azula’s voice was low and malicious, exactly how she needed it to be. “Now.”

Jet turned around, laughing. “Or what? You’ll take a step towards me. Please. I’ll shoot before you can even flick your wrist. And then this White Lotus scum will be gone.”

“Azula, just leave!” cried Ty Lee. “I can fight him! You don’t care about me enough to risk your life!”

Hearing Ty Lee say that made Azula’s heart break, but she kept her attention focused on Jet, who was still laughing. “If you don’t care about her, why the *fuck* are you here?”

“She’s wrong,” replied Azula, keeping her tone menacing, but allowing her eyes to meet Ty Lee’s. “I care about her very much.” She glared at Jet, staring him directly in the eyes. “And I *won’t* let you hurt her.”

She had no idea how she’d managed to move so fast, and perhaps it was because Jet hadn’t expected her to move at all, but in a flash, *she* was standing behind *Jet* , holding her knife to his throat. “Don’t move a muscle,” she hissed.

Jet laughed. “What are you going to do to me? I’ll still shoot her. Even if you kill me for it. She’s White Lotus scum, just like everyone else here.?”

“You wish,” hissed Azula, pressing the dagger into his throat. “What I’ll do to you will be much *worse* than death. This city is full of dangerous, deadly, murderous criminals; you know that better than anyone.” She laughed, and could feel the wind making her choppy blangs whip around. “And *me* ? I’m what those deadly criminals, the deadliest in the world, are afraid of. They *run away* from me. So,” she said, leaning in even closer to him, “do you really want to see the full extent of what I can do?”

Jet froze for a moment, then slowly dropped his gun and released Ty Lee. The gun fell over the side of the balcony, and Ty Lee dropped to the floor, panting.

Azula wasted no time, turned, and smashed the handle of her dagger over Jet’s head. His eyes rolled back in his head, and he crumpled to the balcony, nearly falling over the railing.

In a flash, all of the adrenaline left Azula’s body. Her legs buckled under her and she dropped to the floor, exhausted.

She felt arms wrap around her, and, against her will, tears started streaming down her face. She looked up into Ty Lee’s wide eyes, and found herself at a loss for words.

“That was amazing!” cried Ty Lee. “You were like some sort of badass superhero! And wow, I had no idea you could be so intimidating! It was so cool!” Her eyes softened, and she squeezed Azula’s hand, making Azula blush against her will. “Thank you.”

Azula wanted to leap off the balcony right then and there.

How could she have shown the girl she was trying to protect such a monstrous side of her? This was the power-hungry side of her that had murdered Zhao. This was the side that had been brought out by *torture* .

“I’m sorry,” she managed to get out between gasps and sobs. “I...I’ve been trying to protect you from this. I’m not what you think I am. I’m not the kind of person you get close to.” She took a deep breath. “I’m damaged, Ty Lee. I was labelled a monster when I was a child. My father raised every part of me to be exactly like him, and he was... *awful* . *I’m* awful.” She sighed. “I tried not to care at all, but the truth is, I care about you too much to subject you to that. So I’ve been trying to keep it away from you. I can be terrifying sometimes, and I *knew* that, and I tried not to show that part of me to you, and what do I do? I terrorize someone right in front of you. I’m so sorry.” She had never felt like such a mess in her life. “I wish it were different, but…”

She was interrupted when Ty Lee wrapped her arms around her, leaned forward, and kissed her.

Azula was still crying, and there was a part of her brain that was screaming at her to pull away, but the longer they kissed, the more every cell in her body was wishing for it not to stop. It was perfect.

“Azula,” said Ty Lee, hugging her tightly the second they broke apart, “have you been trying to protect me from yourself this whole time? Because you think you’re too damaged?”

“I don’t think,” sighed Azula, still crying, “I know.”

“Don’t be silly,” whispered Ty Lee, wrapping her arms around her again. Azula’s face felt like it was on fire. “I know you’re perfect exactly how you are. No matter how you see yourself.”

She kissed her again, and this time, every part of Azula was telling her not to let go.

## Chapter 34: The King of Clubs

### Notes

#### Chapter Summary

A new interrogation session reveals important information, and puts the events of the past two weeks in a different light in the eyes of Zuko, Azula, and Katara.

#### Chapter Notes

Sorry for not updating yesterday! School is starting for me in a few days, and the combination of anxiety and generally being tired has left me lacking a little bit in motivation to write and post. I'm still trying my hardest to finish by the end of the month, so fingers crossed that I can manage that! Bear with me!

TW: Threats, knives, physical assault, blackouts.

Happy reading!

### Text

“Let’s take this from the top,” said Zuko, pacing back and forth in Iroh’s office. Next to him stood Azula, Sokka, and Katara, and behind the desk sat Jet, who had his hands tied behind the chair he was sitting in, and looked absolutely livid. “Who hired you, and why did you try to kill Ty Lee?”

At the very mention of Ty Lee’s name, Azula’s entire face turned a deep shade of red, even deeper than it had turned before, and a small smile spread across her face, though she quickly masked it under a serious façade. *Interesting* . Zuko would have to ask her about that later.

“Why should I answer you?” snapped Jet. He nodded towards Azula. “That girl just held a knife to my throat and hit me over the head.”

“You were about to murder my girlfriend.”

*Girlfriend* ? Well, *that* was *definitely* interesting (though not exactly unexpected.)

Jet let out a harsh laugh. “Fair enough.”

“And I’m still not above cutting your throat if you don’t tell us everything you know.”

There was something about Azula that had become different since her torture at the hands of Zhao and Long Feng. She seemed a little more...ruthless. It reminded Zuko a little bit of the Azula from his childhood, but also completely different. Did that make any sense? It made no sense.

“Stop it!” snapped Katara, rolling her eyes. She turned to Jet. “Jet, it doesn’t have to be like this. We all understand why you do what you do. You’re a kid, like us, and you’ve had a lot of *really* bad shit happen to you. It doesn’t excuse what you did, but we’re not going to kill you.”

“You could,” said Jet in a flat tone. “It wouldn’t make much of a difference.”

In that moment, seeing the usually furious, reckless Jet quiet and looking completely lost, it was almost as though Zuko was looking at a reflection of his past self in a mirror. The effect was disorienting.

Katara sighed. “Jet, please. I know you’re a good person. You have good intentions. You just want to stop bad people from doing bad things. I believe that there’s a better life out there somewhere for you. But you need to understand that hurting innocent people like Ty Lee isn’t a good thing, and you need to help us stop other innocent people like her from getting killed. More than eight people are already dead. Please don’t let that number get any higher.”

Jet stared out the window for a moment, sighing. “Fine,” he said quietly after a moment. “But you need to untie me.”

“What?” snapped Sokka. “No! You just tried to murder one of our best friends! Of course we’re not going to untie you!”

“Untie me, or you don’t get any of the information you’re looking for,” said Jet with a smirk, leaning back in the chair and kicking his feet up on the table. “That’s the deal. You want me to start respecting the lives you claim are human? Fine. But you need to do the same for me.”

Azula glared at him. “You’re not lying. But that doesn’t mean I’m putting this away.” She brandished her dagger in front of them. “I’ve had a really bad day, and I’m not going to be tricked into any more disasters.”

“Paranoia,” scoffed Jet. “Seems fitting for you.”

Azula said nothing, but shot him a glare as she pointedly looked away.

“Well, I’m leaving,” said Sokka. “If he starts trying to kill all of you, yell, and I’ll be right outside so that he can’t get all of us.”

“You know, if he kills us all before we call for help, he could very easily take you by surprise and kill you, too.”

“That’s not the point, Azula!” Sokka shot one last suspicious glare at Jet before he stomped out of the room.

“Close the door behind you,” laughed Jet. Sokka stuck out his tongue at him before slamming the door so hard that the doorframe shook.

“I really hope we haven’t just signed off on our own death,” said Azula as she went behind the desk and sliced neatly through the ropes binding Jet’s hands.

“Don’t worry,” said Jet, leaning forward onto the desk. Beneath his cocky exterior, there was a shred of sincerity starting to appear that surprised Zuko. “You haven’t.” He glanced at Zuko. “You’ve been awfully quiet for a detective. Don’t you have any questions?”

“I’m still waiting for you to answer my first questions,” replied Zuko. “Who hired you, and why did you try to kill Ty Lee?”

“I don’t know who hired me,” Jet said with a sigh.  
“That’s preposterous,” laughed Azula. “How could you not know who hired you? Is there a website for assassins?” Her voice oozed sarcasm.

“Actually,” said Katara, “that’s *not* the most unrealistic thing I’ve ever heard.”

“There’s no website for assassins,” said Jet, rolling his eyes. “But about a week and a half ago, an envelope of money showed up on my windowsill, with a note that told me I’d get the other half if I killed a squadron of Dai Li guards. I’d never killed anyone before, but I hated the Dai Li, and I needed the money, and I lived in Assassin’s Lane, so I knew where to find the right weapons and how to get to the Dai Li mansion.” He gestured to Azula. “You found those bodies. I remember hearing you from the vents.” He laughed. “They deserved it.”

“Jet,” said Katara, with a sad but reproachful tone of voice, “those were real people. They were guards. They were just doing their job.”

“Their *job* was working for an organization that stole from, experimented on, and tortured innocent people! They may be people, but they’re not innocent.”

“Neither are you,” said Zuko. “Everyone thinks they’ll be justified if they decide to kill. Maybe they are, and maybe they aren’t, but if nobody ever draws a line, the whole world descends into chaos. I don’t disagree with you that these people are despicable, and maybe we’d be better off without them, but that’s not your decision to make, and nobody has the right to take someone else’s life in cold blood. Which brings me to my second question.” He leaned forward. “Why did you try to kill Ty Lee?”

“ *Don’t* try to say she was just White Lotus scum,” snapped Azula from behind him. “You met her. You *knew* what kind of person she was when you stepped onto that balcony. Nobody could know that and still believe that she was worthy of killing.”

“It wasn’t my idea,” replied Jet. Slowly, he reached into his pocket and pulled out a wrinkled piece of paper. “Earlier today, this showed up in my apartment.”

Katara took the note and opened it. “The White Lotus will never stop leaving innocent people behind for their own selfish gain. The only way to truly make them stop is to…” she glanced up “to take an innocent of their own. Do it tonight, or else this cycle will never end.” She glanced up at him. “Jet, did something happen?”

“You *know* what happened,” hissed Jet. “I found their little box of secrets when I was escaping this place after I tried to kill that old wrestler. Some of them are murderers, criminals, thieves, just like me, but they’re all getting away with it.”

“They’ve changed!”

“ *I* could change if anyone ever gave me the chance! But the White Lotus has crafted this city so that people like me never get that chance. They *need* to be stopped.”

“You’re right,” said Katara. “And when this is all over, I promise you we’ll work on this. But right now, people are dying. And whether or not they’re truly innocent, the city is in danger. We need to focus on stopping it.”

Jet sighed. “I wish I could help,” he admitted, and Zuko got the feeling that he was telling the truth.

“You already have,” said Katara with a smile.

“Let me see that note,” said Zuko. As he looked at it, both Katara and Azula peered over his shoulder.

“Interesting choice for a murderer,” mused Azula. “If I were planning to hire an assassin, I would type my note so that no one could ever identify my handwriting. And this is easily identifiable handwriting. Look how utterly sloppy it is!”

“I think that’s on purpose,” said Zuko. “This can’t be the writer’s natural handwriting. It was probably written with their non-dominant hand.”

“That’s a clever way to cover your tracks,” said Azula. “I should think about that sometime.”

“If a stranger walked into this room,” said Jet, “they would probably think that you were the murderer and not me.”

Azula smirked. “And that is perfectly fine with me. If I’m more fearsome than the killers, then the killers fear me. I still win.”

Jet rolled his eyes. “Is she always like this?”

“Yes,” said both Zuko and Katara.

“Look at the strange marking over that *i* ,” said Azula, turning back to the note. “It looks somewhat like a flame.”

“What? No!” said Zuko. “It looks like a lotus blossom.”

“I don’t know,” said Katara. “It looks more like a bear claw to me.”

Suddenly, it felt like a lightning bolt went off in Zuko’s head. He turned to Azula. “Do you think Arnook and Hama had notes like these, too?”

“I’m not sure,” she replied, pulling out her dagger and examining it closely. “If they did, I have no idea where we’d find them.”

“Wait!” cried Katara. “Hama’s shawl fell off while she was attacking everyone at the party! I bet it’s still here!”

“I wonder if any of Arnook’s things are here, too,” wondered Zuko, getting to his feet. “Sounds like we’re going on a scavenger hunt.”

“Wait,” came Jet’s voice from behind them. Jet looked Katara in the eyes. For the first time since they’d met him, he looked scared. “What are you going to do with me?” His voice sounded defeated, as though he was already positive that the absolute worst was going to happen. It was a feeling that Zuko knew well.

The three of them looked at each other. Zuko could see from the expressions on Azula and Katara’s faces that neither of them knew the answer, either. After a moment of silence, it was Katara who walked over to the desk and sat across from Jet. “Look, Jet, I think the truth is...we’re not sure.” She reached across the table and squeezed his arm for a second, and Jet looked so surprised that he nearly jumped out of his chair. “You’re young. You’ve got good intentions. You’ve been hurt, and you aren’t malicious. I *really* want to give you a second chance.”

“You won’t regret it.” Jet’s voice sounded slightly eager, and slightly desperate. Even Azula, who Zuko was sure despised Jet with every aspect of her being after what he’d done to Ty Lee, looked conflicted at the sound of it.

“But here’s the thing,” said Katara with a sigh. “I think it has to wait a while. We can’t afford to worry about you betraying us at all, even if I don’t think you’re going to, until whoever hired you, whoever hired all of these people, is locked up.”

“Whoever it was will kill me for telling you all of this.”

“We won’t let them,” said Katara. “Look, I think the best thing for you to do is stay here. You’ll be safe, and we’ll be able to…” she sighed “keep an eye on you. And maybe you can meet some of the White Lotus members.”

“I’d rather die.”

“Be my guest,” snapped Katara. “But maybe if you talk to them, you’ll realize that they’re human, too. They’ve just made mistakes. Like you.” She stood and crossed over to the doorway. “Thanks for your help, Jet.”

Zuko closed the door behind them, and locked it.

“Here’s Hama’s shawl,” said Katara as they reached a storage closet on the fifth floor, pulling out a black-and-white checkered shawl. “I remember how it was flying when she threw her knives.” She glanced at Zuko and Azula. “You guys were in the tunnels during most of that.”

“Speaking of the tunnels,” said Zuko, as Azula ran her fingers over the fabric of the shawl, “how are you doing with the whole Yon Rha thing?”

“What does that have to do with the tunnels?”

“The tunnels were where we found the White Lotus’s box, which is where we found Yon Rha’s confession of your mother’s murder.”

Katara blinked, slightly confused, then sighed. “I don’t know. It’s sort of nice knowing that the man who was vicious enough to take my mother’s life away is dead, and at the same time, I’m just so glad it wasn’t me who killed him.” She sighed. “Does that make me a horrible person?”

“Not at all,” replied Zuko. “It's one thing to want people dead. Whether or not we admit that to each other, we all have someone. It’s whether or not you act on it, and how, that determines how bad the action is.”

“But what if I had? Would I have been a bad person then?” Katara sighed. “Sorry, are we talking about this too much? I can stop.”

“Stop it,” said Zuko. “I was the one who asked. And to answer your question, I’m not sure it’s so easy to define good and bad people. Everyone’s experience is different, and every victim and killer has a different story. If you had killed him, I don’t think you’d have been a bad person. You’re still Katara. You were still protecting people.”

“What about whoever we’re chasing?” mused Katara. “How do we know they’re not trying to do that, too? The White Lotus and the Dai Li are kind of messed up.”

“They are,” admitted Zuko, “but this person, whoever they are, is worse than you could ever be. They’re killing repeatedly. You can see it’s planned, not fuelled by emotion or trauma. They’re killing people for no specific reason other than belonging to certain groups. A lot of them haven’t even committed any crimes. They’re truly innocent, and this person killed them. To top it off, whoever this is has been roping so many people into this murder spree, people who would have otherwise been innocent.” He placed his hand on her shoulder. “That’s a million miles away from going after a known murderer because you’re rightfully furious.”

Katara smiled. “Thanks, Zuko.”

“I hate to interrupt this little philosophy session,” said Azula from the other side of the coat closet, “but you two might want to look at this.”

She held Hama’s shawl in one of her hands. In the other was a crumpled note. Even from across the cupboard, Katara could see that the handwriting was the same as Jet’s note.

Azula read the note aloud. “The White Lotus is having a party tonight. You know what to do. Or else your family line will die out.”

“Hama’s family was killed by the White Lotus and the Dai Li when she was young,” said Katara. “She was desperate not to be killed by them so that she could live out their legacy and die naturally, like they should have. Whoever wrote this must have known that.”

“What a manipulative bastard,” mused Azula, in a tone that was a combination of disgust and admiration. Katara didn’t know whether to laugh or be concerned. Probably both. She turned to Zuko, who had started rummaging in the back of the closet. “What are you doing back there, Zuko?”

A moment later, Zuko emerged from a pile of coats, clutching a thick, blue, corduroy jacket with giant brown buttons and grey fur lining the collar. “I think this was Arnook’s,” he said.  
“How do you know that?” asked Azula. “Did he have a preference for grey furs, or corduroy? Are there fragments of his hair scattered all over the shoulders? Is there an oil stain on the wrist that matches a cologne that only he uses?”

“How many murder mystery novels have you read?” said Zuko. Katara had to admit that she was rather astonished, too. “Azula, his name is literally written on the tag.”

“Oh,” said Azula, her face turning slightly red. “Yes, I suppose that also makes some sense.”

Zuko dug through its pocket. “And look!” he cried. “There’s another note!”

“Whoever hired these people was rather careless,” mused Azula. “These notes are all over the place.”  
“I don’t think they expected their carefully chosen assassins to get caught,” said Zuko.

“There’s a picture of Chief Song attached to this note,” Katara pointed out. She read aloud. “Kill the man responsible for your best friend’s death, or else a killer will roam free forever. He tricked him! This is awful!”

“No surprise there,” muttered Azula.

“It’s clever, though,” said Zuko. “Whoever hired all of these different assassins was setting up a line of defense. If any of them got caught…”

“They could be framed for all the murders!” finished Katara. “Or they could frame one of the other assassins, since there were so many of them! I bet whoever hired these people never actually killed anyone themselves.”

“It’s still a rather impossible line of defense,” mused Azula. “If this is truly a fake handwriting, then whoever wrote these notes will never use it in front of us, even if we test every single citizen in town for their handwriting. And none of the killers we’ve caught so far know who hired them, or they’re too scared of them to admit it.”

“Based on these notes, I don’t blame them,” said Katara. “But does this mean what I think it means?”

“That depends,” said Azula. “What do you think it means?”

“It means,” said Zuko, “that we’re close to figuring this out. *Really* close. But we’re stuck. Again.”

After listening at the door for about ten minutes, just to be absolutely sure that Jet wasn’t going to murder his friends, Sokka wandered down the stairs and into the lobby. After Jet’s discovery, the White Lotus had stopped the party they’d been in the middle of throwing, and all four members, plus three of the four White Lotus children had gone to bed (Sokka could faintly hear Ty Lee bouncing on her bed, even from six floors down.) The mansion was eerily silent.

In fact, it was so late at night that the enormous chandelier that usually provided the light for the ballroom was extinguished, and the only light was coming from small torches on the walls. For an organization that claimed to be good, that was a pretty environmentally unfriendly thing to do.

Instinctively, Sokka reached into his back pocket and grabbed the handle of his boomerang. He didn’t know why, but maybe it was the atmosphere of a dark, deserted mansion late at night that made him feel like he might need it.

He wished he lived here. If he lived at the White Lotus mansion, maybe he’d know where the light switches were.

A small beam of light snaked over towards his feet. His gaze followed it, and soon, Sokka was standing in front of a coat closet.

“Someone must have left the light on in here,” he muttered to himself. “Even more environmentally unfriendly.” He gripped his boomerang even tighter and fully ready to throw it into the door as hard as he could if someone tried to lock him inside. Once inside the closet, he began leafing through the various coats and grazing his hand over the wall, wondering where the fuck the light switch was.

In the back of the closet, there was an extra row of coats that he had to reach through, and he sort of had to lean his head into the coats to reach all the way towards the wall. As he reached all the way back, he thought he heard something rustling behind him.

*It’s probably just the coats* , he thought. *Everyone’s asleep at this point* .

He found no light switch, but as he was pulling his hand back out, his fingers got caught in one of the coat’s pockets.

“Damn it!” he muttered to himself, eventually having to reach into the rack and pull the coat out in order to unhook his fingers from its pocket. The coat in question was deep red, and in neat writing on the tag was written the name *Piandao* .

“Stupid coat,” he muttered, and was about to slide it back onto the rack when his hands brushed against something inside its pocket. Confused, he reached all the way inside and pulled out a small scrap of paper.

He shouldn’t have been going through Piandao’s belongings, but he couldn’t help it. He was too curious.

Unfolding the scrap of paper revealed the most sloppily-written note Sokka had ever seen in his life. What was the dot over the *i* supposed to be, a paint splatter? But the most surprising thing was what it said.”

Sokka read over the words again and again. He couldn’t believe what he was seeing.

If Piandao had a note like this, then that meant…

Something hard hit Sokka over the back of the head. As his knees buckled, he swung his boomerang frantically, trying to think of something to do to save himself.

And then everything faded away.

### End Notes

#### Chapter End Notes

Yes, another cliffhanger. It's a murder mystery, and I have a thing for cliffhangers. I'm sorry, I know it doesn't have to be like this.

Anyway, if you've got something to say, please leave me a comment or come talk to me on Tumblr at @theatergirl06:)

## Chapter 35: The Love Detectives

### Notes

#### Chapter Summary

The clock is ticking as the group investigates another disappearance, but Zuko has his own complicated feelings to work out.

#### Chapter Notes

Okay, this one was super fun to write, so I hope it's fun for y'all to read, too:)

TW: Freezing cold, swords.

### Text

Zuko yawned as the group headed down the stairs. “Why does it always seem like we’re up late, and every time we’re about to go to sleep, a new bad thing happens that keeps us up until three in the morning?” asked Katara as they entered the darkened lobby, after going through the rest of the upstairs closets and confirming that there were no more notes hidden in old boxes or coats.

“Occupational hazard of the job,” murmured Azula. “Can we please hurry up and get home now?” She addressed this last comment to Zuko, who was standing in the middle of the lobby and looking around. “We’re not going to find anything else tonight, and we need to sleep. You’re the one who gave me the atrociously long speech about not neglecting my physical health for the sake of this case.”

Zuko barely heard her. It had only just struck him that something wasn’t quite right about the lobby (or the ballroom, depending on what the White Lotus was using it for at any given moment.) In other words, something was missing. “That’s not what I was thinking,” he murmured to himself. He turned to face the two girls. “Do either of you know where Sokka is? He said he was going to wait out here.”

The two girls exchanged a worried glance, and Zuko could feel the anxious feeling settling over the entire group. “I wouldn’t worry too much about it,” said Katara, whose anxious gaze betrayed her words. She was right. Normally, Zuko wouldn’t worry too much about it. But these weren’t normal times. “He probably just went home once he realized that Jet wasn’t going to kill us. It *is* late.”

“Without leaving a note or texting?” said Zuko. “That’s not really like Sokka. This is the guy who once called me because he was stuck in traffic and was going to be five minutes late to our meeting. He’s like you,” he said to Azula. “Besides, he knows what’s going on right now. He wouldn’t leave without saying anything.” Just like the night before, he couldn’t shake the feeling that something was wrong, and if even one one-hundredth of what had happened to Azula happened to Sokka...Zuko wasn’t completely positive that he could take it.

“I’ll text him,” said Katara, whipping out her phone. “If he’s on the train home, he’ll see this, and he’ll answer, and everything will be fine.” It was obvious from her voice that she was trying her absolute best to sound calm, but the more she spoke, the more her worry came through into her words.

It felt like the three of them stood still, staring at Katara’s phone, for an hour. Zuko could feel his heartbeat getting faster and faster with every second they waited.

“He’s not answering,” said Katara after ten minutes or so. “And unless there’s school, Sokka’s *really* good at answering his phone. I have a bad feeling about this.”

If something happened to Sokka…

He couldn’t even bring himself to think about it.

“Let’s not jump to conclusions,” said Azula, who, as usual, seemed the least frantic out of the three of them, but not in an apathetic sort of way, which Zuko appreciated. The Azula he remembered from his childhood would have been much worse. Then again, perhaps he’d just seen her in a different light back then. “We should search the mansion before we assume the worst. It’s absolutely possible that he wandered into one of the rooms, got distracted, and isn’t checking his phone.”

“Or he could already be dying!” snapped Zuko. He could feel an anxious, protective adrenaline rising through his body, and it was making it very hard for him to stand still. “And we’ll be wasting our time!”

“If he’s dying already, we need to find him!” said Katara. “Azula’s right. Searching the mansion is our best shot.”

“Then run as fast as you possibly can,” said Zuko, and he sprinted off towards the library on the third floor.

Why would anyone want to hurt Sokka? What could he have possibly done?  
It felt like eternity as Zuko tore through room after room. He had forgotten what thinking was like; all he could feel was worry and adrenaline as he moved through the mansion. In a haze, he pulled clothes out of drawers and threw them onto the floor, opened every cabinet, and smashed plates on the floor. He even swam to the bottom of the pool, and emerged soaking wet but empty-handed. He felt almost dizzy. Every single room he visited, he turned into a chaotic mess, leaving no stone unturned, and looking for clues in places where they couldn’t possibly be. He knew he was being irrational, and he didn’t care. If there was something in this mansion that was going to help him find Sokka, he was going to do *absolutely everything* in his power to get it. No holding back, no playing it safe. If Sokka truly was in danger, they couldn’t afford to take that chance.

He occasionally passed Azula or Katara, who were also searching the house (though in a much less panicked manner than Zuko.) Both of them were looking more worried by the minute. The longer they searched the mansion, and the longer they came back with nothing, the more sure Zuko was that there was something *very* wrong.

After an hour of going through every room in the mansion, the three of them met back in the lobby, exhausted and even more anxious than when they’d started searching.

“He still hasn’t answered his phone,” said Katara. “Have either of you heard anything?”

Zuko shook his head, and Azula did the same. “Why would anyone want to hurt Sokka?” wondered Zuko. He turned to Azula. “The Dai Li was looking for information when they kidnapped you, but we defeated them. Any information that Sokka has, the White Lotus could get easily.”

How could anyone wish harm on Sokka? Zuko couldn’t stop asking himself. Sure, Sokka could be annoying and overly sarcastic, but he was loyal, smart, and friendly, and his jokes were even sometimes funny. He was...amazing.

Zuko had never been so glad that no one could read minds. If Katara and Azula could read his thoughts right then, he would have never heard the end of it.

It was then that a bright light from the corner of the lobby caught his eye. “Did anyone check that coat closet?” asked Zuko. Both girls shook their heads, and Zuko walked towards it. “Someone forgot to turn the light out,” he muttered, entering the closet and looking around for a light switch. Whoever had made light switches *so* hard to find had really been a *complete* idiot.

He froze, staring at the floor.

“You’re gonna want to see this.”

Both girls walked over and looked over his shoulders. Katara let out a gasp and clasped her hands over her mouth.

Zuko knelt down and picked up Sokka’s boomerang, which was lying in the middle of the closet floor. It felt strange to hold it in his hands, but it filled him with a deep worry that cut like a knife. It felt like Sokka’s ghost was standing in the room with them, and with every second that he was still gone, its image was fading away.

“Sokka *never* goes anywhere without his boomerang,” said Katara in a shaky voice, after a moment. “If we weren’t already absolutely positive that something was wrong, this confirms it. There’s *no way* he just left this here.”

“Look at its angle,” said Azula, crouching down on the floor next to Zuko, who was still in a haze, staring at the boomerang’s handle. She jabbed him in the arm, hard. “Snap out of it, loverboy. Staring at Sokka’s boomerang like you’ve seen a ghost isn’t going to get him back, so stop floundering in your own anxiety and pitifully unresolved romantic feelings, and *focus* .”

Annoyingly, she was right. Zuko didn’t completely understand everything she’d just said, but he could worry about that later.

*Romantic feelings? Had these been romantic feelings all along? Was that why the thought of Sokka* *getting hurt or killed made Zuko feel so awful? And if they were, did Sokka feel the same way?* *Could he?*

“Look at this angle,” repeated Azula, placing the boomerang. “It doesn’t look as though he was about to throw it. If anything, it looks as though he was pointing it towards that wood panel.” She leaned closer to examine it. “I don’t see anything.”

Zuko stared at the boomerang for a moment, then let out a gasp. “That’s because it doesn’t face that way,” he said, turning the boomerang over. “Sokka’s ambidextrous, which means he could have just as easily been using his left hand to point to that panel there.” He ran his fingers over the wood, but stopped when his hand grazed a part of the wood riddled with deep gashes. He squinted, but in the semi-darkness of the closet, he couldn’t read what was carved in the wall. He *did* only have one fully functional eye, after all.

“Katara, can you read whatever’s carved into the wall?”

Katara crouched down next to him and pointed her phone into the shadows. “That’s Sokka’s handwriting!” she cried. A moment later, her face fell. “That doesn’t make any sense,” she murmured. “I don’t believe it.”

“What does it say?” snapped Azula from behind him, clearly annoyed at not being able to see.

Katara glanced up at them, worry and confusion in her eyes. “It’s messy. Almost like it was written in a hurry.”  
“It probably was.”

Katara’s eyes were wide. “It says *Piandao* .”

It was like all of Zuko’s worry disappeared in a flash and was completely replaced with something new: determination.

If they were right, then Piandao had taken Sokka somewhere, and Zuko *could not* let him kill him.

It was weird to admit, but a world without Sokka was impossible and...heartbreaking to imagine. What that meant for Zuko, Zuko didn’t know, but he couldn’t let that world become a reality. He refused to let that world become a reality. He would die before he let that happen. He was sure of it.

Slowly, he got to his feet, clutching Sokka’s boomerang in his hand. This was going to end tonight.

Maybe he was being dramatic, but Zuko wasn’t good with logic or compartmentalizing. He just...thought what he felt, and right now, what he felt was something enormous and confusing and very, *very* dramatic indeed.

“Piandao has a fencing studio in the Middle Ring. If he’s hiding Sokka somewhere, that’s a good first guess.”

“Then that’s where we’ll go,” said Katara, standing up. She wore a determined expression almost identical to Zuko’s.

Zuko didn’t even realize he was sprinting until he was already out the door and running down the street. Around him, the entire city became a blur. He could see nothing, hear nothing, feel nothing but his heart pounding as he ran, and he could think of nothing but his goal.

*I won’t lose him. Not now, not when I’ve only just let him in.*

Zuko didn’t even completely realize how he knew where Piandao’s fencing studio was, only that he was soon standing in front of it, panting with complete exhaustion. Had he really run all this way? It was sort of hard to believe.

*Don’t give in to exhaustion now. Sokka could be dying.*

Clenching his fists so hard that he thought he felt his skin break, Zuko kicked the door as hard as he could. The door flew off its hinges and went smashing into the back wall. Zuko blinked, surprised at his own kick.

If Sokka was here, he wondered if he’d seen it.

“Stop admiring your own strength like an idiot and get inside!” snapped Katara, who, along with Azula, was standing right behind him.

“Right,” muttered Zuko, quickly hurrying inside the studio. “Sorry.”

There were no lights on inside the studio. It took Zuko a moment to adjust to the darkness, but once he did, there wasn’t much to see. A front room with a desk and a closet where (he supposed) students would put their street clothes while they trained, and behind the desk, a back room with a mat for a floor, where (he assumed) students trained.

“Sokka?” called Katara. “Are you here?”

There was no answer, and the group moved further back into the room with the mat for a floor. Zuko could feel every single one of his senses on high alert, partially because of instinct, partially because he knew he absolutely *could not* afford to fail.

The studio was completely deserted. White uniforms and weapons lined the walls, all of them perfectly straight and pinned up. The uniforms looked so human-like in the dark that Zuko almost thought there were actual humans pinned to the walls, watching him. The only light in the entire room came from the small skylight in the middle of the ceiling.

“Sokka?” Zuko called. “If you’re here, *please* answer us.” He tried to keep the desperation out of his voice, but it showed anyway.

“I’m afraid your friend can’t answer,” came a cold voice from the corner of the room. Zuko whirled around, and Piandao stepped into the light. “He’s been unconscious for a while now, if he’s lucky.”

Zuko didn’t even realize he was moving, but in a flash, he’d grabbed two weapons off the wall and was pointing them at Piandao. They felt strangely comfortable in his hands, as though he’d been a master of them in another life. Odd. “Tell us where he is, *now* .” His voice was shaking with anger, and he didn’t quite recognize the fiery, explosive fury that was building up inside him. All he knew was that he *needed* to get Sokka back. So he hung onto that.

“I’m sorry.” Piandao sounded genuine. “I didn’t want to hurt any of you. But your friend discovered a little secret of mine that I couldn’t afford to let come to light. I had to do what I hoped I never would.”

“Did you kill him?” Zuko’s voice was low and quavering, but crackling with dangerous energy and rage. “You son of a bitch.” He had never felt so cold, or spoken so coldly, in his life.

“Calm yourself,” said Piandao. “He’s not dead. Yet. Unfortunately, the three of you will be dead soon, if you don’t leave now and forget this ever happened.”

“I have a better idea,” said Katara. “If you’re going to kill us anyway, why don’t you tell us what you didn’t want Sokka to find instead?”

“Give us the satisfaction,” added Azula, her voice dripping with disdain.

Piandao sighed. “I guess it’s the least I could do. All right, look, I’m not proud of this, but...somebody hired me to kill Ukano.”

“Ukano of the Dai Li,” hissed Zuko, keeping his weapons raised and pointed at Piandao. “Why would you kill him?”

“You saw what the Dai Li did to us,” snapped Piandao. “They murdered my best friend, made another friend of mine a killer, and accused a girl who grew up with me and my friends of being a killer. I was looking for some way to right their wrongs, avenge us, when I received a strange note. Your friend found it. It told me to kill Ukano, and, well...the rest is history.”

“How can you talk so calmly about this?” snapped Katara. “You’re a monster.”

“I never wanted to,” said Piandao defensively. “What’s done is done, and now I must do whatever I can to protect my secret, no matter how extreme. I’m sorry.” He seemed sincere, which somehow made him even scarier.

“How did you kill Ukano?” asked Azula, her tone flat.

“I froze him to death,” replied Piandao. “I have...access to a deep freezer. One that can drop to unimaginable lows. It’s...left over from the previous owners of its building.”

“Ukano was found in an alleyway near this place,” murmured Zuko. “How did no one figure that out in the first place?” Looking up, he suddenly noticed the faint outline of a door in the back wall. Was Sokka right in front of them? How much time did he have left?

They needed to get to that door, and *fast* . But Piandao was standing in their way.

Zuko was going to fix that.

Slowly, turning every ounce of his energy towards his determination to save Sokka, he raised his weapons and pointed them directly at Piandao’s throat. “Now, listen closely.” His voice was lower than usual, and more sinister. It reminded him a little too much of his father, but he kept going. “You’re going to let us through to that door behind you, which I think leads to that freezer you just mentioned.  
“And if I don’t?” said Piandao calmly.

“Then I cut off every part of your body with these swords, and trust me when I say that I am desperate. Someone I care about a lot...more than anything else, is behind that door, and I am not going to stop until I *get him back* . Even if you have to pay with your life.”

Piandao let out a laugh. “With those weapons? You don’t even know how to use them.”

“You’d be surprised,” said Zuko, faking confidence, still running on determined adrenaline. “I’m capable of the greatest things when I’m pushed to the absolute limit.”

He swung the swords sideways and charged at Piandao. Piandao raised his blade, but Zuko didn’t stop. If he got impaled, so be it. He wasn’t leaving Sokka to freeze to death. It wasn’t an option. He could do anything else in the world, but that wasn’t an option.

*It hadn’t been an option for a while,* realized Zuko.

At the last second, Piandao ducked out of the way of Zuko’s charge. Zuko kept running towards the wall, and, unable to stop, raced up the wall and flipped over, swords still swinging. He had no idea where this adrenaline and skill had come from, all he knew was that he needed to get Piandao out of his way.

Piandao hadn’t been ready for Zuko’s flip, so, as Zuko raced forward for the second time, he swung his two weapons simultaneously, and smashed Piandao over the head with the blunt sides of the blades. The swordsman crumpled to the floor, and Zuko stood over his unconscious body, panting.

“Word of advice,” he hissed, leaning down to make sure Piandao was really unconscious. “Don’t *ever* get in my way when I’m protecting someone important.”

He stayed crouched down for a moment, in a haze of his own power.

“Wow, Zuzu,” said Azula from behind him. Both she and Katara were staring at him. “I must admit, I didn’t know you had it in you.”

At the sound of her voice, Zuko snapped from his haze and raced towards the door in the back, hoping and praying with every inch of his body that he was right, and Sokka was really there.

He pulled on the door as hard as he possibly could. He pulled until he felt the knob scraping the skin between his fingers, until he felt them bleeding, until he felt soreness and pain enveloping his entire lower arms, until he couldn’t even feel his hands anymore.

The door swung open, and a blast of absolutely frigid air hit Zuko head on. A small beam of moonlight from the skylight shone through the doorway, revealing an all-white, freezing room. In the back left corner of the room sat Sokka, his arms wrapped around his knees, staring forward with a blank expression on his face. There were pieces of frost on his eyelashes, and Zuko wasn’t sure if he knew he was there at all.

“Sokka!” Overwhelmed with relief, Zuko plunged into the freezer without thinking, ignoring the cold, and dragged Sokka’s almost limp body out onto the floor. Once out of the freezer, Sokka’s eyelids fluttered, and he looked up at Zuko with a smile.

“You know,” said Katara’s voice from behind them, “I just remembered that Azula and I actually have something very important to do, so...um...we’ll just be in the next room if you need us.”

“Very, *very* important,” echoed Azula. Zuko could hear the two of them giggling all the way into the next room.

Still feeling overwhelmed, but now in a good way, Zuko turned back to Sokka and wrapped his arms around him, pulling him tightly towards him, half-supporting his weight. “I was so scared we wouldn’t be able to find you,” he murmured.

“Well,” laughed Sokka. Did he sound nervous? “I’m pretty easy to find.” Zuko could still feel his teeth chattering. “But...you were worried about me?”

Zuko pulled away, surprised. “Of *course* I was. Did you...did you not think I would be?” Did Sokka think he was cold and heartless? When, in truth, he cared about him more than almost anyone else?

“Well,” said Sokka, his teeth still chattering. His tone was light, but his eyes were serious, and told a completely different story. “I guess I just...you were always saying that we weren’t best friends, and then you got so focused on the case, and I didn’t really think I’d be that important, so I was just sort of going to wait in the freezer and…” he was interrupted as Zuko hugged him again. It had been a long time since Zuko had really hugged anyone, but he couldn’t think of any other way to express the incredibly complicated mess of emotions inside of him.

“Sokka,” he said, pulling away again. “There’s no one more important than you.”

With Zuko’s arms around Sokka’s shoulders, their faces were suddenly very close together, closer than they’d ever really been before. Zuko could feel his heart beating faster with every second they stayed so close to one another.

Sighing, Zuko pulled away, but kept his hands on Sokka’s shoulders. He wasn’t ready to let go, not yet.

He could march into a fencing studio, grab two weapons off the wall, face down a master, do a literal backflip, and hit him over the head, all to save his...someone.

So why was *this* so scary?

### End Notes
